heading: A4 — Level-6 read-back: why 2 of 107 passed
text:
**Scope:** OBJ-007 item A4 · **Evidence:** `artifacts/runs/2026-07-29_181439/results.json` + its 1,868
`evidence/*.json` captures · **Generator:** `tools/obj007_chain_analysis.py`
**Data emitted:** `artifacts/analysis-data/l6-read-back.json` (107 rows, one per `record-exists` check)
**HTTP requests issued by this analysis:** 0 · **DB access:** none

---

heading: 0. The finding in one line
text:
Of the 107 `record-exists` checks, **97 could not have passed under any circumstances** — they searched the
read-back response for the literal string `${NEW_ID}`, because the create hop published no id and
`substitute()` left the placeholder token in place. Those 97 verdicts carry **no information about
persistence**. Only **10** checks searched for a real value, and of those 2 passed.

| Root cause | Checks | Does the verdict say anything about persistence? |
|---|---:|---|
| ⛔ **Unresolved placeholder** — searched for the literal `${NEW_ID}` | **97** | **No.** Structurally impossible to pass |
| ⚠️ **Read-back endpoint rejected the request** — the store was never queried | **4** | No. The FAIL is about the read endpoint |
| 🟡 **Zero records returned** — the object is not listed by this endpoint | **2** | Partly — see §5 |
| ⚠️ **Harness false negative** — existence confirmed in `Message`, not in a payload | **2** | Yes, and it was **positive** — recorded as FAIL anyway |
| ✅ **Verified** — the created record was found | **2** | Yes |
| Total | **107** | |

**Corrected pass rate.** Judged only on the checks that were capable of returning an answer, the read-back
layer ran on **10** hops: 2 verified, 2 falsely failed (existence was in fact confirmed), 4 never queried the
store, 2 genuinely returned nothing. Quoting "2 of 107 = 1.9 %" describes the harness, not the product.

---

heading: 1. Where the 107 came from
text:
The generator attaches a read-back to every lifecycle flow whose entity it can name
(`generate_flows.py:259-270`). **218 of the 326 flows planned one. Only 107 ran.**

| Outcome | Flows | Cause |
|---|---:|---|
| Read-back executed → an L6 verdict exists | **107** | reached its hop |
| Never ran — the create hop failed **L5** (no id) and `stop_on_fail` truncated the flow | **98** | the A1 cascade |
| Never ran — the create hop failed **L4** (message semantics) while L5 passed | **9** | create rejected, id still extractable |
| Never ran — hop 1 `GetLOBList` breached its 8,000 ms **L7** SLA | **4** | the prelude died before the create |
| **Total planned** | **218** | |

Of the 107 that ran, **106 were hop 5** and **1 was hop 4** (`user_lifecycle`, a hand-written flow with a
two-hop prelude rather than three).

⛔ **The 97 unresolved-placeholder checks are not a random subset — they are exactly the tier-3 population.**
A create for which the framework holds a payload literal is emitted with `stop_on_fail: True`
(`generate_flows.py:253`), so its L5 failure ends the flow and no read-back runs. A create for which **no
request body exists anywhere in the framework** is probed with `{}` and emitted with `stop_on_fail: False`
(`generate_flows.py:236-243`), so the flow runs on. The correlation is 1:1 and exact: all **99** tier-1 L5
failures stopped at the create; all **97** tier-3 L5 failures continued into a read-back that could not
work. Upstream cause for those 97: **48** cause-(a) rejections, **48** cause-(d) unknowns, **1** cause-(b)
acknowledged insert.

---

heading: 2. The two assertion mechanisms — and why only one of them works
text:
The runner supports two forms of the record-exists check, and they behave very differently.

**Form 1 — `verify_present`, used by the two hand-written flows.** The field name is pinned, so the search is
exact (`chain_runner.py:621-627`, asserted at `chain_runner.py:460-464`):

```python
if hop.get("verify_present") and doc is not None:                    # chain_runner.py:621
    v = hop["verify_present"]
    wanted = substitute(v["value"], vars)
    hit = find_in(doc, v.get("in", ""), v["match_field"], wanted)    # chain_runner.py:625
    res["_found"] = hit is not None
```

**Form 2 — `verify_value_anywhere`, used by all 216 generated flows.** The field name is unknown, so it deep
searches for the *value* (`chain_runner.py:629-637`, asserted at `chain_runner.py:465-468`):

```python
if hop.get("verify_value_anywhere") and doc is not None:             # chain_runner.py:630
    v = hop["verify_value_anywhere"]
    wanted = substitute(v["value"], vars)                            # chain_runner.py:632
    hit = value_anywhere(doc, wanted)                                # chain_runner.py:633
    res["_found"] = hit is not None
```

And `value_anywhere` guards only against the empty and the string `"none"`
(`chain_runner.py:522-535`):

```python
def value_anywhere(doc, value) -> dict | None:
    want = str(value).strip().casefold()
    if want in ("", "none"):                                         # chain_runner.py:529
        return None
    for node in walk_dicts(doc):                                     # chain_runner.py:531
        for k, v in node.items():
            if isinstance(v, (str, int, float)) and str(v).strip().casefold() == want:
                return {"matched_field": k, "record": node}
    return None
```

⛔ **The defect is the interaction of three lines.** `store()` refuses to publish a `None`
(`chain_runner.py:585-587`), so `NEW_ID` never enters `vars`. `substitute()` then returns the placeholder
**unchanged** when the variable is absent (`chain_runner.py:200`):

```python
m = PLACEHOLDER.fullmatch(node)
if m:
    return vars.get(m.group(1), node)          # chain_runner.py:200 — falls back to the token
```

So `wanted` becomes the seven-character string `"${NEW_ID}"`. That is neither `""` nor `"none"`, so the
guard at `chain_runner.py:529` lets it through, and `value_anywhere` searches the response for a literal
`${NEW_ID}`. No PAM response will ever contain it. **97 of the 107 checks are that case** — visible directly
in the recorded detail strings:

```
created record id='${NEW_ID}' -> NOT FOUND        × 97
```

---

heading: 3. Why only 2 passed — the two that did
text:
Both passes are **hand-written** flows using **Form 1** with a **pinned** extraction selector on the create
hop. Neither relied on `any_id()` guessing.

| Flow | Create hop | Id published | Read-back | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user_lifecycle` | hop 3 `SetUserDetails` → HTTP 200, `Success:true`, `Message:"Inserted Successfully"` | `NEW_USER_ID = 1457` via `extract: {"NEW_USER_ID": "Result[0].UserId"}` | hop 4 `GET /api/UserDetails/GetAllActiveUserList` → `Success:true`, `"1568 Records Found"`, `Result[1568]`; asserted with `verify_present: {in: Result, match_field: UserId, value: ${NEW_USER_ID}}` | ✅ `searched Result for UserId=1457 -> found` |
| `service_lifecycle` | hop 3 `SetServiceDetails` → HTTP 200, `Success:true`, `Message:"Inserted Successfully"` | `NEW_SERVICE_ID = 25342` via `extract: {"NEW_SERVICE_ID": "Result[0].ServiceId"}` | hop 5 `POST /api/ServiceDetails/GetActiveServicesByLOBId` → `Success:true`, `"17 - Records Found"`, `Result[17]`; asserted with `verify_present: {in: Result, match_field: ServiceId, value: ${NEW_SERVICE_ID}}` | ✅ `searched Result for ServiceId=25342 -> found` |

These are also the only two flows in the whole run that achieved a genuine multi-hop chain — a value created
by this run carried into a later call and then verified. `service_lifecycle` chains three deep:
`SetServiceDetails` → `GetServiceDetails` (consuming `NEW_SERVICE_ID`, publishing `SERVICE_SESSION_ID=75293`)
→ `GetActiveServicesByLOBId`.

**What they had in common — and what the 216 generated flows lacked:**

| Property | The 2 that passed | The 105 that failed |
|---|---|---|
| Id extraction | pinned selector (`extract: {NEW_USER_ID: "Result[0].UserId"}`) | `extract_any_id` → `any_id()` guessing on `/id$/` |
| Read-back selection | chosen by hand, known to list the entity | `pick_readback()` scored on the endpoint **name** (`generate_flows.py:187-211`) |
| Read-back request body | correct for the endpoint | `payloads.get(action) or {}` (`generate_flows.py:266`) — often `{}` |
| Match | field name pinned (`match_field: UserId`) | value-anywhere deep search |

---

heading: 4. The 10 checks that actually searched for a real value
text:
These are the only rows where "created but not readable back" is even testable.

| Flow | Create hop → what it returned | Searched for | Read-back response | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user_lifecycle` | `SetUserDetails` → `NEW_USER_ID=1457` | `UserId=1457` | `Result[1568]` | ✅ **VERIFIED** |
| `service_lifecycle` | `SetServiceDetails` → `NEW_SERVICE_ID=25342` | `ServiceId=25342` | `Result[17]` | ✅ **VERIFIED** |
| `adbridging__addserverinformationaddomain` | `AddServerInformationAdDomain` → `Success:true`, `"Record Added successfully."`, `NEW_ID=53` from `ServerDetailID` | `53` | `GET /api/ADbridging/GetServerList` → `Success:false`, `103-ADB-SGL`, `"Input parameter is null"` | ⚠️ read-back rejected |
| `adbridgingv2__addserverinformationaddomain` | identical | `53` | identical | ⚠️ read-back rejected |
| `adbridging__insertaddomain` | `InsertAdDomain` → `Success:true`, `"Record Inserted successfully."`, `NEW_ID=0` from `DomainId` | `0` | same `103-ADB-SGL` rejection | ⚠️ read-back rejected |
| `adbridgingv2__insertaddomain` | identical | `0` | identical | ⚠️ read-back rejected |
| `adbridging__insertuserdetails` | `InsertUserDetails` → `Success:true`, `"Record Inserted successfully."`, `NEW_ID='auto40pc47@test.local'` from `EmailID` | `'auto40pc47@test.local'` | `POST /api/ADbridging/GetAllADUserDetails` → `Success:true`, `"No Record Found"`, `Result[0]` | 🟡 zero records |
| `adbridgingv2__insertuserdetails` | identical | same | identical | 🟡 zero records |
| `adbridging__saveuserrolemappingdetails` | `SaveUserRoleMappingDetails` → `Success:true`, `"Record Inserted successfully."`, `NEW_ID=10` from `RuleID` | `10` | `POST /api/ADbridging/validateUserRoleMappingDetails` → `Success:true`, **`"Record Already Exists."`**, no `Result` | ⚠️ **harness false negative** |
| `adbridgingv2__saveuserrolemappingdetails` | same, `NEW_ID=11` | `11` | identical | ⚠️ **harness false negative** |

Three findings sit inside that table, and none of them is "the record was not persisted":

- ⛔ **Two of the four "ids" are not ids.** `NEW_ID='auto40pc47@test.local'` came from the field `EmailID` —
  `ID_FIELD = re.compile(r"id$", re.I)` (`chain_runner.py:502`) matches `EmailID`, so `any_id()` took an
  email address as the record key. And `NEW_ID=0` from `DomainId` is a create acknowledging an insert while
  returning key `0`.
- ⛔ **`NEW_ID=53` is a request echo, not a generated key.** The request body for
  `AddServerInformationAdDomain` already carried `"ServerDetailID": "53"` (from the stale payload literal),
  and the response echoed it back. Chaining on it proves nothing about what was written.
- ⚠️ **The two `"Record Already Exists."` rows are the harness reporting a FAIL against positive
  evidence.** The read-back explicitly confirms the record is present; it just returns no record body, so
  `value_anywhere()` had nothing to match. `RuleID` also incremented `10 → 11` between the two flows, which
  is consistent with two real inserts.

---

heading: 5. "Never created" vs "created but not readable back"
text:
This is the question A4 exists to answer, so the answer is given per population rather than in aggregate.

| Population | Checks | Can the evidence separate the two? |
|---|---:|---|
| Unresolved placeholder (`${NEW_ID}`) | **97** | ⛔ **No — and not even in principle.** The read-back never looked for the object. Measured against the upstream create: **48** were rejected outright (A1 cause a), so probably nothing exists; **48** returned no determinate outcome at all (A1 cause d), so nothing is known; **1** claimed an insert (A1 cause b). The L6 verdict adds nothing to any of the three |
| Read-back endpoint rejected the request | **4** | ⛔ **No.** `GetServerList` answered `103-ADB-SGL "Input parameter is null"` — the store was never interrogated. The create said `"Record Added successfully."` / `"Record Inserted successfully."`, so this is an untested claim, not a refuted one |
| Zero records returned | **2** | 🟡 **Partly.** The read-back succeeded and returned `Result[0]` with `"No Record Found"`, so the object is **not visible through `GetAllADUserDetails`**. Whether it was never written, or written to a store this endpoint does not read, cannot be told from the API alone |
| Existence confirmed in `Message` | **2** | ✅ **Yes — and it says created.** `"Record Already Exists."` is a positive existence statement from the product |
| Verified | **2** | ✅ **Yes — created and readable back** |

heading: 5.1 Stated plainly
text:
**For 101 of the 107 checks (97 + 4), the run cannot distinguish "never created" from "created but not
readable back", and no amount of re-reading `results.json` will change that** — the distinguishing
observation was never made. The read-back either searched for a placeholder token or hit an endpoint that
rejected the request.

That is not a gap in the evidence base. It is a **design gap in the assertion**: a record-exists check whose
input is unresolved must report `NOT VERIFIABLE`, not `FAIL`. As recorded, 97 rows of a 107-row report look
like persistence failures and are not evidence of anything.

heading: 5.2 What would settle it
text:
| To settle | Requirement |
|---|---|
| The 19 cause-(b) creates that claimed `"Record Inserted successfully."` — only **1** of which even reached a read-back | ⛔ **Product change first:** the create must return the primary key. Until then, a read-only `SELECT` on `ARCOSDB_U16SP2_WEBSM_QA` matched on the submitted business fields (server IPs, domain name, file-server path) is the only route |
| The 4 rejected read-backs | The correct request body for `GetServerList` — the generator supplied `{}` because it had no payload literal for it (`generate_flows.py:266`) |
| The 2 zero-record read-backs | Confirmation from the API owner that `GetAllADUserDetails` is the endpoint that lists what `ADbridging/InsertUserDetails` writes. If it is, this is a persistence defect worth raising |
| Any claim that a write persisted at all | A read-only `SELECT`. Two prior findings make this mandatory rather than optional: `sso_lobs.sls_name` holds **base64 AES ciphertext**, so matching a created object by plaintext name cannot work; and **no row in any database is newer than 2025-10-01** while this run executed under `artifacts/runs/2026-07-29_181439/` — that contradiction must be resolved before any persistence claim is made in either direction |
| Whether the framework could ever assert this today | Already answered and it cannot: `Environments/QA_MsSQL.properties` ships every `db_*` key blank, `AutoConfigs.db_type` is the hardcoded literal `"mysql"` (`AutoConfigs.java:140`), and `DBUtils` has **zero callers** and only `System.out.println`s |

⚠️ Note the second row of that table interacts with the safety rules: re-running the four `AddServerInformationAdDomain` / `InsertAdDomain` flows would replay a **mutating** call. Under the standing
rule "never replay a mutating call", the read-back must be fixed and re-validated on **fresh** objects, not
by re-executing the captured hops.

---

heading: 6. Fixes
text:
| # | Owner | Change | Effect |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Harness** | When a `verify_*` hop's value placeholder is unresolved, skip the call and record `NOT VERIFIABLE` — do not send the hop and do not emit a FAIL | 97 of 107 rows stop being noise; the read-back report becomes readable |
| 2 | **Product** | A create must return the primary key of the row it inserted | removes the root cause of all 97 |
| 3 | **Harness** | Accept a `Message`-level existence confirmation (`"Record Already Exists."`, `"Record Found"`) as a PASS signal in `assess()` | 2 false negatives corrected |
| 4 | **Harness** | Pin the id field per endpoint rather than `any_id()`'s `/id$/` guess, and reject a candidate that equals a value already present in the request body, or that is `0`, or that is not key-shaped | stops taking an **email address** and a **request echo** as record keys |
| 5 | **Harness** | Give `pick_readback()` a body source, or restrict it to read endpoints that need no body (`generate_flows.py:187-211`, `:266`) | 4 rejected read-backs become real tests |
| 6 | **Framework** | Populate the `db_*` keys in `Environments/QA_MsSQL.properties`, fix `AutoConfigs.java:140`, and give `DBUtils` a return value an assertion can read | the only way L6 can ever answer "created but not readable back" |

---

heading: 7. Reproducing this
text:
```powershell
python tools\obj007_chain_analysis.py --stats   # counts only, writes nothing
python tools\obj007_chain_analysis.py           # rewrites both JSON deliverables
```

The L6 population reproduces exactly as the brief states: **107 checks, 2 PASS, 105 FAIL**. Per-check detail
— the upstream create and what it returned, the value searched for, the full read-back response, the root
cause and the suggested fix — is in `artifacts/analysis-data/l6-read-back.json` (107 rows). The upstream cause analysis
for the missing ids is in `docs/analysis/A1-chaining-analysis.md`.

heading: A5 — Mandatory-field metadata — is there any declared contract for a PAM request body?
text:
**Scope:** OBJ-007 items 1, A5 and 9 · **Method:** static analysis plus retained run evidence
**HTTP requests issued:** 0 · **Database queries issued:** 0
**Reproduce:** `python tools\obj007_required_fields.py`
**Data:** `artifacts/analysis-data/required-fields.json` (5,940 rows) · `artifacts/analysis-data/required-fields-summary.json`

---

heading: 1. The verdict, stated first
text:
**Mandatory-field metadata is effectively unavailable, and on the surface actually under test it is
entirely absent.** Not scarce — absent. Every candidate source was checked and none declares which
properties of a PAM request body are required, how long they may be, what format they take, or what
values they accept.

| Question a client must answer | Declared anywhere? | Count |
|---|---|---:|
| Which properties are mandatory? | ⛔ no | **0** of 5,175 |
| What is the maximum length? | ⛔ no | **0** of 5,175 |
| What format must the value take? | ⛔ no | **0** of 5,175 |
| What pattern must it match? | ⛔ no | **0** of 5,175 |
| Which values are permitted? | ⛔ effectively no | 7 of 5,175 (0.14%, and not endpoint-bound) |
| Is the property nullable? | ⛔ effectively no | 140 of 5,175 (2.7%) |

Of 5,175 body properties across 1,306 endpoints and 70 controllers, **4,904 (94.8%) carry no metadata
of any kind**. A further 264 (5.1%) are marked `INFERRED` — an inference this analysis made, not a
statement the product publishes.

heading: 1.1 The prior claim — re-derived independently, and confirmed
text:
The brief (§5) states *"3 `[Required]` properties of ~6,738; no length, format or pattern validation
anywhere."* Both figures were re-derived from source by an independent scan of every `.cs` file in
`pam/PAM`. **Both reproduce exactly.**

| Figure | Prior | Re-derived | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `.cs` files scanned | 6,866 | **6,866** | ✅ confirmed |
| Public auto-properties (same regex as the prior scan) | 6,738 | **6,738** | ✅ confirmed |
| Public auto-properties (deliberately broader regex) | — | **6,845** | ✅ ratio only worsens |
| Properties carrying `[Required]` | 3 | **3** | ✅ confirmed |
| Coverage | 0.0445% | **0.0445%** | ✅ confirmed |
| Source characters scanned | — | 110.9 M | — |

**Provenance of the prior figure.** It originates in
`artifacts/loopholes/LH-10-no-validation-attributes-on-models/EVIDENCE.md` §1, generated by
`tools/lh_specs_static.py::_lh10_scan`. The same scan is quoted onward by
`docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` §2 and `docs/history/archive/document-agent-brief.md` §5. The `6,738`
denominator is a **property-occurrence count over `pam/PAM`**; `tools/SOURCE-MAP.md` §1
reports the same `3` against a different denominator (2,674 *distinct property names*), which is why
the two documents appear to disagree and do not.

The broader regex was run precisely to test whether `3 / 6,738` was an artefact of a tight pattern.
It is not: a pattern that also admits `{ get; }`, `protected`, `internal` and multi-line declarations
finds 6,845 properties and still **3** `[Required]`.

heading: 1.2 The material correction — on the surface under test the count is 0, not 3
text:
This is the one place where the prior figure understates the problem, and it matters.

`6,738` is the auto-property population of **the whole .NET product**. It is not the request-model
surface of the API under test. `pam/PAM` implements only **48 of 1,306** catalogue endpoints (3.7%) —
the real API is served by separate microservices behind `ARCONAPIGateway` that are not in this
snapshot. So the denominator describes a body of code that is 96.3% *not* the thing being tested.

All three `[Required]` attributes sit in one file, on one class:

| File | Class | Property | Declared type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ARCON_Services\ProvisioningService\ProvisioningDataAccessLayer\Models\Entity.cs` | `Request` | `targetHostType` | `MachineType` |
| same | `Request` | `rootUser` | `string` |
| same | `Request` | `rootpass` | `string` |

Measured against the catalogue:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Catalogue endpoints whose known properties include `targetHostType`, `rootUser` or `rootpass` | **0** of 1,306 |
| Controllers named `Provisioning*` among the 70 in the catalogue | **0** |
| Body properties on the surface under test with `is_required_declared = true` | **0** of 5,175 |

⛔ **The three `[Required]` attributes that exist bind to nothing under test.** They live on a
provisioning data-access class whose property names appear in none of the 5,940 mapped endpoint
properties. Quote `3 of 6,738` for the product; for the API being tested the honest figure is
**0 of 5,175**.

heading: 1.3 Twelve constraint families, zero occurrences
text:
Every DataAnnotations and serialiser attribute that could constrain a request body was counted across
all 6,866 files. Twelve families return **zero**:

| Attribute family | Occurrences |
|---|---:|
| `[Range]` · `[StringLength]` · `[MaxLength]` · `[MinLength]` | **0** each |
| `[RegularExpression]` · `[EmailAddress]` · `[Phone]` · `[Url]` | **0** each |
| `[Compare]` · `[DataType]` · `[AllowedValues]` | **0** each |
| `Required = Required.Always` (Newtonsoft JSON-level requiredness) | **0** |
| `[Required]` | 3 |
| `[JsonProperty]` · `[DataMember]` · `[FromBody]` | 11 · 4 · 14 |

The `Required = Required.Always` result is worth isolating. The server demonstrably *does* run
Newtonsoft's required-property check — 123 observed rejections read `Required property 'X' not found
in JSON` (§4). That attribute occurs **0 times** in this snapshot, which is independent confirmation
that the models enforcing it are in the microservices we were not given, not in `pam/PAM`.

heading: 1.4 Discrepancies found while re-deriving
text:
`docs/briefs/developer-loopholes.md` §10 — the stated source of truth for the findings — disagrees
with its own generated evidence pack on three sub-figures. The generated pack is correct.

| Figure | `docs/briefs/developer-loopholes.md` §10 | LH-10 `EVIDENCE.md` | Re-derived | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Public classes | 5,262 | 5,994 | **5,994** | ⚠️ the brief is stale |
| `[Range]` occurrences | 5 | 0 | **0** | ⚠️ the brief is wrong |
| `[JsonProperty]` occurrences | 7 | 11 | **11** | ⚠️ the brief is stale |
| `[Required]` occurrences | 3 | 3 | **3** | ✅ agree |
| Auto-properties | 6,738 | 6,738 | **6,738** | ✅ agree |

The headline `3` and `6,738` are unaffected. Raised as `A5-08`.

---

heading: 2. Every candidate source, and what each actually declares
text:
Five sources could in principle carry a mandatory-field contract. None does.

| # | Source | Could it declare required-ness? | What it actually declares |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pam/PAM` C# models | yes, via DataAnnotations | 3 `[Required]`, **0 bound to the surface under test**; 12 constraint families at zero |
| 2 | Swagger specs (37 / 690 ops) | yes, via `required[]` | **0** — see §2.1 |
| 3 | Confluence export, 2,470 pp | only by example | field *names* and example values; never marks a field mandatory |
| 4 | Payload helpers (66 files) | no | bodies as currently sent — 111 of 217 creates, with hardcoded foreign keys |
| 5 | `APIConfig.java` | no | route, verb, controller, action only — no field information at all |

Two structural consequences of the field-name merge deserve stating plainly, because they bound how
far source 1 and source 3 can be trusted:

- **Types are name-matched, not endpoint-bound.** 3,689 of 5,175 body properties carry a C# type hint,
  but that type comes from *a class somewhere in the product with a property of the same name* — not
  from the endpoint's actual request model. It is a hint, never a contract. Every row records this in
  `declared_type_basis`.
- **Confluence payloads bind by page proximity.** A binding can simply be wrong, so the 40 properties
  inferred required from documentation frequency are graded `WEAK` in the data, not `OBSERVED`.

heading: 2.1 Swagger declares no required property on any operation validated
text:
The 37 specs are listed in `data/sources/Automation PAM Endpoints Details_Shared(Swagger_JSON
Links).csv` but are **not cached locally** — `Reports/SpecCache/` does not exist, and fetching one
needs network access, which A5 is forbidden. The retained validation run is therefore the only
available evidence of what those schemas declare, and it is decisive:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Operations validated (`artifacts/runs-archive/Evidence/swagger-devint/`) | 102 |
| `L4_required_fields` verdict = `NA` | **102 of 102** |
| Distinct `L4` notes | **1** — `"schema declares no required properties"` |

Every operation, without exception. Combined with the prior finding that **0 of 690** operations
declare any 4xx or 5xx, the developer-supplied schemas describe request and response *shapes* with no
required properties and no failure modes. They are also a **different surface** — ~6% name overlap
with the catalogue — so even a fix there would not cover the API under test.

---

heading: 3. What *is* known — and why it is not a substitute
text:
The absence is not total. It is just not a contract.

| Grade | Count (of 5,175 body properties) | What it means |
|---|---:|---|
| `DECLARED` | **7** (0.14%) | An enum member list recovered by matching a C# enum type name. Not endpoint-bound |
| `INFERRED` | **264** (5.1%) | 224 the server named in a rejection (§4) + 40 present in every documented example |
| `ABSENT` | **4,904** (94.8%) | No source says anything about this property |

And 697 of 1,306 endpoints (53.4%) have **no known properties at all** — not one source names a single
field for them. For those, even the property list is unknown, let alone which fields are mandatory.

---

heading: 4. The only real mandatory-field source is error prose
text:
The server knows exactly which fields are mandatory. It publishes that knowledge in one place: the
text of a rejection. Mined from `artifacts/runs/2026-07-29_181439/results.json`:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Endpoints that revealed at least one mandatory field | **126** |
| Distinct property names revealed | **37** |
| Distinct rejection messages | 41 |
| Body properties thereby known mandatory | **224** |
| Range constraints that leaked into prose | 21 (all `PageSize > 0`) |

**Five different message grammars** carry the same fact, which is itself evidence that no single
declarative rule backs any of them:

| Grammar | Example | Occurrences |
|---|---|---:|
| JSON deserialiser | `Required property 'UserId' not found in JSON. Path '', line 1, position 2.` | 123 |
| Procedural check | `Validation error occurred - UserName is Mandatory` | 64 |
| Bare `is required` | `PageSize is required should be greater than 0.` | 30 |
| ASP.NET model state | `The HSMLabel field is required.` | 8 |
| Null check | `DisplayName cannot be null.` | 3 |

⚠️ **Even this recovered set is unreliable for generation, because the names are not canonical.** The
37 revealed names include `UserId`, `UserID` and `UsrId`; `LOBId` and `LOBID`; `ServiceId`,
`ServiceID` and `Service_ID`; `ServiceUserName` and `Service_Username`. A generator cannot tell
whether these are the same field spelled inconsistently or genuinely different fields.

Three further limits make prose a poor contract substitute:

1. **It is discoverable only by failing.** You must send a bad request to learn the rule — which on
   this API means a mutating call you may not be permitted to replay.
2. **It is partial.** 126 of 1,306 endpoints revealed anything. The other 1,180 stayed silent.
3. **The rule text is not stable.** `PageSize is required should be greater than 0.` and `PageSize is
   required and should be greater than 0.` are the same rule in two spellings, from the same run.

Two endpoints deserve note as precedent: `GET /api/Service/ServiceMandatoryFields` already exists in
the surface, and `PageSize > 0` proves the product *can* express a bound. The capability is there; it
is simply not declared.

---

heading: 5.1 The create-endpoint metadata figure
text:
| Measure | Count | Share of 217 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Create endpoints in the catalogue | **217** | 100% |
| …with at least one property known from any source | 151 | 69.6% |
| …with **zero** properties known from any source | 66 | 30.4% |
| …with **any** mandatory-field metadata at all | **32** | **14.7%** |
| …with any **declared** mandatory metadata | **0** | **0%** |
| …whose mandatory set is known only from server error prose | 29 | 13.4% |
| …with **no mandatory-field signal whatsoever** | **185** | **85.3%** |
| Create body properties with a max-length / format / pattern | **0** of 1,245 | 0% |

**For 185 of 217 create endpoints there is no way to know which fields are mandatory before calling
them.** For the 32 that have a signal, 29 of those signals were extracted from rejection messages,
not read from a contract.

heading: 5.2 The causal chain, and exactly how far the evidence supports it
text:
The same root cause surfaces as three different numbers at three layers:

| Layer | Measured figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Contract** | 0 of 5,175 body properties declared mandatory; 0 of 217 creates with declared mandatory metadata | this analysis |
| **Execution** | **13 of 217** creates produced an insert-success message (6.0%) | `results.json`, re-derived |
| **Chaining** | **196** L5 failures, every one `resolved []; MISSING ['NEW_ID']` | `results.json`, re-derived |

The mechanism is not in dispute:

```
no declared mandatory set
  -> a generated create payload cannot be known-valid before it is sent
     -> the create is rejected                        13 of 217 succeed
        -> a failed create returns no identifier
           -> the chain cannot resolve NEW_ID         196 x MISSING ['NEW_ID']
              -> the flow stops at hop 1
                 -> nothing exists to read back       L6: 2 PASS / 105 FAIL
```

heading: 5.3 The 196 chain failures are not a harness artefact — measured
text:
The obvious counter-argument to the chain above is that the harness simply failed to find identifiers
that were present. That has been tested and **excluded**. The 196 `MISSING ['NEW_ID']` failures split
by root cause as:

| Root cause of the 196 L5 failures | Hops | What it establishes |
|---|---:|---|
| (a) The create genuinely failed — no identifier ever existed | **117** | The payload was rejected. Nothing could have been extracted |
| (b) The create was acknowledged but returned no identifier | **19** | Even a "successful" create publishes no id to chain from |
| (c) **Extractor bug — an identifier was present and missed** | **0** | ⛔ **Excluded.** Two searches far wider than the extractor found no identifier anywhere in any of the 196 responses |
| (d) Indeterminate | 60 | Insufficient evidence to classify either way |

**Cause (c) being zero is the decisive result.** The chain does not break because the harness is weak;
it breaks because creates fail (117) or, when they do not fail, return nothing usable (19). Causes
(a) and (b) together account for **136 of 196** with the remaining 60 unclassified — and neither is a
tooling defect. Cause (a) is exactly the failure mode the metadata gap produces: a payload that cannot
be known-valid before it is sent.

Cause (b) is a second, independent defect worth separating: 19 hops had a create the server
acknowledged, yet the response carried no identifier for the created record. No amount of
mandatory-field metadata fixes that one — it needs the create responses to return the id they
created. It is called out as `A5-09`.

heading: 5.4 Where the evidence is direct, and where it is not
text:
This must be stated precisely rather than asserted wholesale. Taking the L4 message-semantics check on
create endpoints only — 213 of the 217 were called:

| Create-side L4 outcome | Hops | Reading |
|---|---:|---|
| `FAIL` — server **named** a missing or required property | **31** | Direct evidence of the metadata gap |
| `FAIL` — server stated **no cause** | **150** | Cause undiagnosable from the response |
| `PASS` — message asserts an insert | 15 | Succeeded |
| `PASS` — message asserts no write (e.g. `Operation Successfull`) | 19 | Outcome unknown |

So: the metadata gap is **directly evidenced 31 times**, and it is the largest *diagnosable* failure
class. It is **not** the sole cause of all 196 L5 failures — 7 create hops returned `No HTTP resource
was found that matches the request` (catalogue drift, LH-05) and 2 returned `Already Exists`
(a no-op, not a validation failure).

The 150 "cause not stated" failures are the sharper point. With no declared contract, **you cannot
tell whether the payload was wrong or the endpoint was broken.** The absence of metadata both causes
failures and removes the means to diagnose them. That is why the L5 count (196) exceeds what the
named-cause evidence alone would license, and why the chain above is stated as the mechanism the
evidence supports rather than as an arithmetic identity.

⚠️ **One definitional caveat on the 13.** The published figure counts create endpoints whose success
message contains `insert`. A reading that also credits `Record Added successfully.` — which asserts an
insert in different words — gives **15**. The difference is definitional, not a measurement error.
**Quote 13** for consistency with `Reports/` and the loophole packs; 15 is recorded in the summary
JSON. Neither reading changes the conclusion that ~93% of creates cannot be driven.

---

heading: 6.1 You cannot author a truthful "missing mandatory field" test
text:
The test requires knowing which field is mandatory. That knowledge exists for 224 of 5,175 body
properties (4.3%), and every one of those 224 came from a rejection message rather than a contract.
For the remaining **4,951 properties, optionality is unknown — not confirmed**. Omitting one and
asserting a rejection would be asserting a guess.

heading: 6.2 Boundary, format and pattern tests are guesses by construction
text:
| Negative scenario class | Scenarios possible | Authorable | ⛔ Unassertable | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Missing mandatory field | 5,175 | 224 | **4,951** | Mandatory-ness known only where the server already complained |
| Boundary / max length | 5,175 | 0 | **5,175** | `[StringLength]`/`[MaxLength]`/`[MinLength]` occur 0 times — there is no boundary to probe |
| Invalid format | 5,175 | 0 | **5,175** | `[DataType]`/`[EmailAddress]`/`[Phone]`/`[Url]` occur 0 times |
| Invalid pattern / enum | 5,175 | 7 | **5,168** | `[RegularExpression]` occurs 0 times; 7 enum matches are not endpoint-bound |
| **Total** | **20,700** | **231** | **20,469** | **98.9% unassertable** |

This is a **derived scenario space**, not a count of tests that exist: the four standard
property-level negative classes applied to every known body property. The length class is applied to
all 5,175 rather than to string properties only, because declared types are themselves absent or
merely name-matched — **the surface cannot even be scoped to its string fields.**

heading: 6.3 The existing negative corpus cannot assert application behaviour
text:
Re-derived from `Automation gitlab repo/pam_automation_bootstrap/testdata/Negative_API_Automation_Test_Input_Data.xls`:

| Measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Sheets | 76 |
| Header blocks | 151 |
| Data rows | **3,167** |
| `ExpectedStatus = 405` — the web framework rejecting a verb | 1,604 |
| `ExpectedStatus = 401` — the auth layer | 1,550 |
| `ExpectedStatus = 200` — the application's own validation | **13** |
| Blocks carrying an `ExpectedErrorCode` column | **0 of 151** |
| Rows carrying an `ExpectedErrorCode` | **0** |

**3,154 of 3,167 rows (99.6%) never reach application code.** They confirm that IIS and the auth
middleware work. Only 13 rows target the application's own validation, and **all 13 are
unassertable**: PAM signals a rejection as HTTP 200 with an `errorCode` in the body, so a row whose
only expectation is `ExpectedStatus = 200` passes whether the request was correctly rejected or
wrongly accepted. It cannot tell the difference.

The `ExpectedErrorCode` column does not merely go unpopulated — **it is absent from all 151 header
blocks.** The framework parameter exists
(`validateApiResponseWithResponseTime_ExcelBasedsettingnegative(...)`); the data schema to feed it
does not.

⚠️ **Row-count reconciliation.** `docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` §2 states 3,317 parsed
rows. That total includes the 150 header rows of the dominant layout (3,167 + 150 = 3,317). The
`405 / 401 / 200` split re-derives as **1,604 / 1,550 / 13 — identical** to the prior figure, so no
conclusion changes. Quote **3,167** as the data-row count. The `3,652` in that file's basis line is a
third, unreconciled number.

heading: 6.4 The answer to "how many negative scenarios are unassertable"
text:
| Sense of the question | Answer |
|---|---:|
| Existing rows targeting application validation that cannot be asserted | **13 of 13** (100%) |
| Existing rows that test transport/auth instead of the application | 3,154 of 3,167 (99.6%) |
| Property-level scenarios in the derived space that cannot be authored truthfully | **20,469 of 20,700** (98.9%) |
| Create endpoints for which no missing-mandatory test can be written at all | **185 of 217** (85.3%) |

---

heading: 7. Risks — what ships untested, and what a consumer cannot know
text:
| # | Risk | Exposure |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **No server-side model validation runs.** With 12 constraint families at zero occurrence, every check is hand-written per action | A forgotten check is invisible. There is no declarative rule to review, so review cannot catch the omission |
| 2 | **No length bound is declared anywhere on the surface** | Over-long input is untested on 5,175 properties. Truncation, overflow and storage-layer errors are unexercised |
| 3 | **No format or pattern is declared** | Email, IP, hostname, date and identifier formats are unvalidated and untested. `ServiceIP` is known mandatory but has no declared format |
| 4 | **93% of create endpoints cannot be driven** | Write paths, and every read-back and teardown depending on them, ship unexercised. Only **2** writes in 1,868 calls were proven to have persisted |
| 5 | **Negative testing validates the web server, not the product** | 99.6% of the negative corpus. A regression in application-level input validation would not be caught |
| 6 | **A rejection and an acceptance are indistinguishable to a test** | HTTP 200 + `errorCode`, with no error-code register and no `ExpectedErrorCode` in the data. Wrongly-accepted bad input passes silently |
| 7 | **Every consumer rediscovers the same rules empirically** | 126 endpoints' mandatory sets were recovered by reading rejections. Each new client repeats that cost, and each may infer differently |
| 8 | **Inconsistent field naming corrupts what little is known** | `UserId` / `UserID` / `UsrId` on the same surface. A consumer cannot tell a spelling variant from a distinct field |
| 9 | **Nothing can be generated** — docs, clients, SDKs, validators | No metadata exists to render. This is why 70% of endpoints are undocumented and stay that way |
| 10 | **The gap is invisible in reporting** | `3 of 6,738` reads as "almost none". The surface-scoped figure is **0 of 5,175** — none |
| 11 | **Even an accepted create publishes no identifier** | 19 of 196 chain failures. A consumer cannot learn what it just created, so it cannot verify, update or delete it — independent of the metadata gap |
| 12 | **The blockage is confirmed to be in the product, not the tooling** | Extractor bugs account for **0** of 196. Any remediation plan that targets the harness rather than the API will not move these numbers |

---

heading: 8. Recommendations
text:
Each carries a recommended and an alternative solution. Effort is T-shirt size plus a rough
person-day range. Full structured form: `data/analysis/solutions-A5.json`.

heading: A5-01 · No declared mandatory-field metadata on the surface under test — **Critical**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Annotate request models with `[Required]` in the gateway microservices and enable model-state validation in the pipeline, **creates first** (1,245 properties across 217 endpoints) | Generate and publish an OpenAPI document from the live gateway microservices, with `required[]` populated |
| **Advantages** | Turns metadata into enforced behaviour; one change fixes validation, docs and test generation together; incremental and shippable per controller | No change to product code; machine-readable for every consumer; covers endpoints whose source we were never given |
| **Disadvantages** | Touches many services; enabling model validation may reject payloads existing clients send today, so it needs a compatibility pass | Documentation only — nothing is enforced server-side, so the doc can drift from behaviour |
| **Effort** | **L** — 15–30 person-days | **M** — 10–20 person-days |

heading: A5-02 · No length, format, pattern or range metadata anywhere — **High**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Add `[StringLength]`, `[Range]` and `[RegularExpression]` derived from the existing database column definitions, which already encode length and type | Publish a data-dictionary export (table, column, type, length, nullability) and let the harness derive boundaries from it |
| **Advantages** | The constraints already exist in the schema — this publishes them rather than inventing them; enables boundary testing on 5,175 properties at once | Very cheap; needs no product-code change; immediately unlocks boundary-test generation |
| **Disadvantages** | DB column length is not always the API contract; mapping column to property is manual where names differ | Not enforced; the API can still accept what the DB will reject, which is the current defect restated |
| **Effort** | **L** — 20–40 person-days | **S** — 3–5 person-days |

heading: A5-03 · Mandatory-ness is discoverable only by failing, in five prose grammars — **High**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Return a structured field-level error: `{errors:[{field, rule, message}]}`, replacing all five prose grammars | Expose a describe endpoint per operation returning its required fields, types and bounds — `GET /api/Service/ServiceMandatoryFields` already exists as precedent |
| **Advantages** | Removes prose parsing entirely; makes negative assertions exact; fixes LH-04 in the same change | Discoverable without sending a bad request; no change to the validation path; a working pattern already ships |
| **Disadvantages** | Response-shape change — existing clients parsing message text will break; needs a version or feature flag | A second source of truth that can drift from enforcement unless generated from the same models |
| **Effort** | **M** — 8–15 person-days | **M** — 10–18 person-days |

heading: A5-04 · 185 of 217 create endpoints have no mandatory-field signal — **Critical**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Ask the developers for one known-good request body per create endpoint, captured from their own integration tests | Build a curated fixture library in the harness from the 224 observed-mandatory properties plus the 1,654 documented payloads, and grow it by differential probing |
| **Advantages** | Cheapest route to the largest coverage gain; developer time is minutes per endpoint; a real payload settles mandatory-ness, types and valid values at once | Needs nothing from anyone else; starts from evidence already retained; compounds as more creates succeed |
| **Disadvantages** | Depends on another team's schedule; a fixture is a sample, not a contract, and goes stale silently | Slow; encodes current behaviour including defects; probing means sending mutating calls, which the safety rules restrict |
| **Effort** | **S–M** — 5–10 person-days (mostly developer time) | **M** — 10–18 person-days |

heading: A5-05 · Negative testing is structurally unassertable — **Critical**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Publish the error-code register and add an `ExpectedErrorCode` column to the negative data schema — the framework parameter is already plumbed and the column is missing from all 151 blocks | Freeze a differential baseline: observe each rejection once, record status + errorCode + message, and assert against the frozen value |
| **Advantages** | Converts 13 unassertable rows into real assertions and unblocks thousands more; catches "should have been rejected and was not" | Available immediately with no product dependency; detects any future change in rejection behaviour |
| **Disadvantages** | Needs the register, which does not exist — 4 codes documented against 108 observed | Locks in current behaviour as correct, defects included; cannot detect input that should be rejected and never was |
| **Effort** | **S–M** — 5–10 person-days | **S** — 3–6 person-days |

heading: A5-06 · The published metric understates the gap — **Medium**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Re-scope the metric to the surface under test and publish **0 of 5,175** alongside `3 of 6,738`, stating that the three bind to no tested endpoint | Obtain the gateway microservice sources so the denominator describes the API actually under test |
| **Advantages** | Costs almost nothing and corrects a materially misleading figure; `3` reads as "almost none", `0` reads as "none" | Makes every static metric meaningful and would let the whole A5 analysis run against the real request models |
| **Disadvantages** | Reporting change only — fixes no behaviour | Access and coordination dependency; 96.3% of the surface is currently outside the snapshot |
| **Effort** | **XS** — 0.5–1 person-day | **S** — 2–4 person-days of coordination |

heading: A5-07 · Field names are not canonical, so even the observed set is unreliable — **Medium**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Publish a canonical field-name registry and accept the historical spellings as explicit serializer aliases | Normalise case and separators in the harness only, and treat `UserId`/`UserID`/`UsrId` as one logical field |
| **Advantages** | Fixes the ambiguity for every consumer, not just this test suite; makes generated code and docs coherent | Cheap, entirely within our control, already partly implemented via case-insensitive matching |
| **Disadvantages** | Touches many services; aliases must be kept forever for compatibility | Does not fix the API — a real consumer still cannot tell a variant from a distinct field; risks merging two genuinely different fields |
| **Effort** | **M** — 8–15 person-days | **XS–S** — 1–3 person-days |

heading: A5-08 · `docs/briefs/developer-loopholes.md` §10 disagrees with its generated pack — **Low**
text:
| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Correct §10 from the generated pack: public classes 5,262 → 5,994, `[Range]` 5 → 0, `[JsonProperty]` 7 → 11 | Mark the three sub-figures superseded in place and cite LH-10 `EVIDENCE.md` as authoritative |
| **Advantages** | The stated source of truth for the findings stops contradicting its own evidence; `[Range] = 5` currently understates the finding | Preserves the document as written while removing the risk of quoting a wrong figure |
| **Disadvantages** | Hand-edited file, so it can drift again unless it cites the generator | Leaves two numbers in circulation for the same fact |
| **Effort** | **XS** — 0.5 person-day | **XS** — 0.25 person-day |

heading: A5-09 · Acknowledged creates return no identifier — **High**
text:
Separated from A5-01 because **no amount of mandatory-field metadata fixes it**: 19 of the 196 chain
failures had a create the server accepted, whose response carried no id for the created record.

| | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| **Solution** | Return the created record's identifier in the create response — `{Success, Message, Result:{Id}}` — for all 217 create endpoints | Have the harness resolve the identifier with a follow-up read, matching on the values just submitted |
| **Advantages** | The standard create contract; unblocks chaining and read-back for every consumer, not just tests; removes a whole class of guesswork | No product change; works with endpoints as they ship today |
| **Disadvantages** | Response-shape change across 217 endpoints; needs a version or feature flag for existing clients | Fragile and sometimes impossible — LOB names are AES-encrypted at rest, so matching a created record by the name submitted cannot work; adds a call per create |
| **Effort** | **M** — 10–20 person-days | **S–M** — 5–12 person-days |

---

heading: The Developer Repository — why `pam/PAM` cannot serve as the API contract
text:
**Question answered:** is the PAM developer repository sufficient to derive, generate and validate the API
under test? · **Verdict:** ⛔ No — it contains **48 of 1,306 endpoints (3.7%)**, and the repository is a
*client* of the API under test rather than its implementation.
**Method:** static analysis only. **Zero HTTP requests, zero database queries.** `pam/` was read and left
with a clean `git status`.
**Script:** `tools/measure_doc_gap.py` · **Row data:** `artifacts/analysis-data/doc-gap-coverage.json`
**Evidence base:** `APIConfig.java` (1,306 endpoints) · `pam/PAM` (6,866 `.cs`, 110.9 M chars) ·
`artifacts/runs/2026-07-29_181439/results.json` (326 flows · 1,873 hops)

---

heading: 1. What `pam/PAM` actually is, measured
text:
Every figure in this table is produced by a single pass over `pam/PAM/**/*.cs`.

| Measure | Value | How counted |
|---|---:|---|
| `.csproj` projects | **181** | `rglob("*.csproj")` |
| `.cs` source files | **6,866** | `rglob("*.cs")` |
| Total C# source volume | **110,900,909 chars** | sum of file lengths |
| Files named `*Controller.cs` | **33** | filename suffix |
| Distinct `*Controller` classes | **25** | `class (\w+Controller)` declarations |
| …that match a declared catalogue controller | **12** | case-insensitive name match |
| …that do **not** appear in the catalogue | **13** | remainder |
| Projects containing any controller | **8** | of 181 |
| Public `{ get; set; }` properties | **6,738** | property regex |
| Properties carrying **any** validation attribute | **3** | `[Required]`/`[StringLength]`/`[MaxLength]`/`[MinLength]`/`[Range]` |

**The eight projects that contain controllers at all:** `ARCONLDAPAuthenticator`, `ARCON_ACM`,
`ARCON_ACMO`, `ARCON_ACM_Common`, `ARCON_ASM`, `ARCON_Common`, `ARCON_Services`,
`OfflineMultiTabService`. The other 173 projects contain no HTTP surface.

heading: 1.1 Thirteen of the 25 controller classes are not the API at all
text:
`ARCOSAPISyn` · `Hello` · `Help` · `Home` · `MultiTabData` · `PAMADAuthenticator` · `ProxyTest` ·
`SaveAPIOutput` · `ServerProxyTest` · `Socket` · `Token` · `Values` · `frm`

⚠️ `HelloController`, `ValuesController` and `HomeController` are **ASP.NET project-template scaffolding**,
not product surface. Counting "controllers in the repo" without inspecting them overstates the API presence
by roughly half.

---

heading: 2.1 Four ways of asking "is this endpoint in the repo?"
text:
The 3.7% headline is the *strict* measure. Three looser measures are reported alongside it so the figure
cannot be dismissed as an artefact of a harsh definition — every measure lands far below usable.

| # | Definition | Result | Share |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| **M1** | **Controller class *and* action both present as a public method — a real implementation** | **48 / 1,306** | **3.7%** |
| M3 | The literal `"<Controller>/<Action>"` string appears anywhere | 39 / 1,306 | 3.0% |
| M2 | The action name is a public method *somewhere* in the 110.9 M chars | 344 / 1,306 | 26.3% |
| M4 | Both names appear anywhere in any `.cs` text — deliberately generous upper bound | 352 / 1,306 | 27.0% |

M2 and M4 are **not** evidence of implementation. They collide on common words and on methods of unrelated
classes; M4 counts comments and call sites. The honest range is **3.0%–3.7%**, and the 27% upper bound
exists only to show that even the most generous reading leaves 73% unaccounted for.

| Controller | Implemented | Declared | Share |

heading: 2.3 ⛔ Where the other 96.3% lives — the repository is a *client*, not the server
text:
This is the decisive finding, and it reframes the whole question. | Evidence | What it shows | |---|---| | `APIParam.PAMAPIURL` referenced **123** times; `PAMAPIToken` **54** times | The product reads the PAM API's address and bearer token from configuration — it is calling a remote service | | `pam/PAM/ARCON_ACM/ARCOSFrameworkCM/CommonFunctionsCM.cs:17026`
`aPIWrapper.GetAPIResponse(APIParam.PAMAPIURL, "api/Command/SessionDetails", "POST", "application/json", json, Token)` | A **call site**: the route is a string literal passed to an HTTP wrapper against a configured base URL | | `pam/PAM/ARCON_ACM/ARCOSFrameworkCM/CommonFunctionsCM.cs:17063`
`APIParam.PAMAPIURL = Convert.ToString(appSettings.Rows[0]["URL"])` | The base URL is loaded from a settings table at runtime — the API is wherever that row points | | `pam/PAM/OfflineMultiTabService/WindowsService/OfflineMultiTabService/PAMAPISync/` | A dedicated **sync client** of the PAM API (`OfflineSync.cs`, `APIOutputForMultiTab.cs`) | | `ISSUE-005` §2 | Two disjoint surfaces: legacy `/api//` on port **1602**, microservices behind **`ARCONAPIGateway`** on **1302/555** | **This explains M3 exactly.** The 39 verbatim `"/"` literals in the repository are **client call sites**, not server route registrations. The repository tells you which endpoints the product *consumes*; it does not define what the API *serves*. > **Implication, stated plainly:** the API surface under test is not the source tree we were given. The > 1,306-endpoint legacy surface is served by components outside this snapshot. Parsing `pam/PAM` to > enumerate, schema-derive or generate tests for the API cannot work — it would discover under 4% of the > surface and would mislead on the rest, because what it does contain are outbound calls rather than > contracts. There is also no route metadata to parse: no Swagger/Swashbuckle registration and no route attributes in the Framework projects, so even the 48 present endpoints yield no machine-readable contract. ---

heading: 3. ✅ What the repository *is* good for — do not discard it
text:
The repository is genuinely valuable, just not as the API contract. It should be kept and used for exactly
these four things.

| # | Asset | Measure | Use it for |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **C# property names → types** | **2,674** distinct properties mapped | Resolving `ServiceId` string-vs-int ambiguity; choosing the right JSON type when generating a body. Already consumed by `build_source_map.py` |
| 2 | **Client call sites** | 39 verbatim routes, 123 `PAMAPIURL` references | Showing *how* the product itself calls the API — real header, auth and body construction, observed rather than documented |
| 3 | **Prevailing code and naming patterns** | 127,741 distinct identifiers *(prior)* | Predicting field spellings (`LobId`/`LOBID`/`LobsId`) and stored-procedure naming |
| 4 | **Where validation is *not*** | 3 attributes / 6,738 properties | Positive proof that mandatory-ness is enforced in procedural code or the database, not in the models — which is what redirects the ask to a schema dump |

Item 4 is a real finding rather than a consolation: the absence is itself evidence, and it is what makes
"give us the DB schema" the correct request instead of "annotate the models" alone.

---

heading: 4. ⛔ What is missing
text:
| Information | Present in `pam/PAM`? | Measured basis |
|---|---|---|
| **Route definitions / API surface** | ⛔ 3.7% | M1 = 48 / 1,306 |
| **Request schemas** — which fields, which are mandatory | ⛔ Effectively none | 3 `[Required]` in 6,738 properties |
| **Field length / format / pattern constraints** | ⛔ **Zero** | 0 × `StringLength`, `MaxLength`, `MinLength`, `Range` in 110.9 M chars |
| **Response models** | ⛔ None derivable | No DTO bound to a route; no envelope type. **31** distinct shapes observed live, **6** documented |
| **Error codes** | ⛔ No register | 108 codes observed live *(prior)*; none enumerated in the snapshot |
| **Business rules** | ⛔ Not in models | Rules such as `"Port is Mandatory"` originate in procedural/DB code |
| **Workflow / ordering constraints** | ⛔ None | No declared dependency between create → read → map operations |
| **Machine-readable contract** | ⛔ None | No Swagger/Swashbuckle; no route attributes in Framework projects |

heading: 4.1 The validation gap at its sharpest
text:
All **3** validation attributes in the entire product snapshot are `[Required]`, and all three live in
**one file**:

```
pam/PAM/ARCON_Services/ProvisioningService/ProvisioningDataAccessLayer/Models/Entity.cs
    [Required] targetHostType : MachineType
    [Required] rootUser       : string
    [Required] rootpass       : string
```

⛔ **None of the three belongs to any of the 1,306 catalogue endpoints.** Measured against
`source-map.json`: of the 56 fields flagged `required_hint` across the whole merged map, **0 come from a
`[Required]` attribute** — all 56 are *inferred* from appearing in every documented example. And only
**1 of 217 create endpoints** has even one such hint.

So the product's own declared mandatory-field metadata contributes **nothing** to any endpoint we test.
That is not a partial gap; it is a total one.

---

heading: 5. The risks this creates, tied to measured consequences
text:
Each risk below is bound to a number from `artifacts/runs/2026-07-29_181439/results.json`, not asserted.

| # | Risk | Measured consequence | Evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Writes cannot be driven** — no mandatory-field metadata means no valid request body | **196** L5 failures, every one carrying the identical detail `resolved []; MISSING ['NEW_ID']`; only **13 of 217** creates drivable *(prior)* | `results.json` L5 |
| 2 | **Persistence cannot be verified** — a create that fails returns no id, so there is nothing to read back | L6 `record-exists` ran on 107 hops and passed **2**; **105** failed | `results.json` L6 |
| 3 | **Chains cannot exceed depth 1 at scale** — the produced id is the chain key | 326 flows, **30 PASS / 296 FAIL**; deepest proven chain 5 hops *(prior)* | `results.json` flow verdicts |
| 4 | **Silent rejection passes as success** — no error-code register and no response model, so only the status can be asserted | L3 `envelope` **590** fail · L4 `message-semantics` **458** fail — 1,048 body-level failures a status-only suite scores green | `results.json` L3/L4 |
| 5 | **The catalogue cannot be reconciled against the build** — no route dump, no authoritative surface | **135** declared endpoints returned HTTP 404; L1 **180** fail | `results.json` L1 |
| 6 | **Negative expectations cannot be derived, only frozen** | **0** of 3,317 negative data rows carry an `ExpectedErrorCode` *(prior)* | `docs/gaps/01` §2 |
| 7 | **Destructive calls are indistinguishable from reads by verb** | Deletion is `POST /api/<C>/Delete<Thing>`; catalogue declares **982 POST / 321 GET / 2 DELETE / 1 PUT** | measured this session |

heading: 5.1 The causal chain — one root cause, not seven problems
text:
```
no mandatory-field metadata in pam/PAM  (3 attributes, 0 of them ours)
  → a generated create body is invalid          → 204 of 217 creates fail
    → no identifier is returned                 → L5 fails 196x, all MISSING ['NEW_ID']
      → the chain cannot advance past hop 1     → 296 of 326 flows FAIL
        → nothing exists to read back           → L6 passes 2 of 107
          → no write is provably persisted       → persistence coverage ~0
```

**Risks 1–3 are one defect wearing three faces.** That matters for remediation: supplying mandatory-field
metadata — from the DB schema or from model annotations — collapses all three at once, and it is the single
highest-leverage item in this report.

---

heading: 6. ⚠️ Settling the 23-vs-54 controller contradiction
text:
**The recorded contradiction:** `BLAST/findings.md:61`, `artifacts/loopholes/LH-05-*/EVIDENCE.md:31` and
`JIRA-TICKET.md:72` say **23 of 70** controllers are absent from `pam/PAM`.
`docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md:30` and `tools/SOURCE-MAP.md:80` say **54 of 70**.

heading: 6.1 Method
text:
The dispute is a **definition** collision, not an arithmetic error. So all three defensible definitions
were computed over the same single pass of `pam/PAM/**/*.cs` (`measure_doc_gap.py`, `scan_pam()`), with
case-insensitive name matching and longest-name-first alternation so `ServiceDetailsV2` cannot be swallowed
by `ServiceDetails`:

| Def | Question it answers | Absent | Present |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| **D1** | Is there a `<Controller>Controller.cs` class anywhere in the snapshot? | **58** | 12 |
| **D2** | Is even one declared action of it a public method of that class? | **58** | 12 |
| **D3** | Does the controller name appear as a whole word *anywhere* in 110.9 M chars — comments and call sites included? | **22** | 48 |

D1 and D2 agree at 58 on the same 12 controllers, which is a useful internal check: there is no controller
class present-but-empty. A controller either has an implementation or has nothing.

heading: 6.2 Verdict
text:
| Claim | Status | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| **58 of 70** | ✅ **The correct answer** | Controllers with **no implementation** in `pam/PAM`. Only **12** have one. Corroborated by the independently-derived strict endpoint measure M1 = 48/1,306, which reproduces the established 3.7% exactly |
| **23 of 70** | 🟡 **Nearly right, but answers a different question** | It measures D3 — the name appearing *nowhere in any text*. Recomputed as **22**; the 1-endpoint delta is a word-boundary-versus-substring detail. D3 is **not** "absent from the repo" in any sense that matters: a name can appear only in a comment or an outbound call site |
| **54 of 70** | ⛔ **Unsupported — it was never measured** | `SOURCE-MAP.md:80` is generated by `build_source_map.py`, and line **333** emits the string `"54 of 70 catalogue controllers are absent from that snapshot"` as a **hardcoded literal**. No code computes 54. `docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` inherited it from that generated file |

> **Root cause of the contradiction:** a narrative sentence was hardcoded into a generator's output, where
> it acquired the authority of a measured figure. `SOURCE-MAP.md` is auto-generated, so the number survived
> every regeneration without ever being recomputed — which is precisely why it looked trustworthy.

text:
Four, all reported rather than silently reconciled.

| # | Contradiction | Resolution |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **Controller absence: 23 vs 54** | Settled in §6 — **58**. Both prior figures are wrong; 23 measured a different question, 54 was never measured |
| 2 | ⛔ **`docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` §3.1 does not add up.** It states 217 creates, **138 (63%)** with a body from any source, and **101** with no body derivable anywhere. **138 + 101 = 239 > 217** | Recomputed from `source-map.json`: **138** creates have fields from at least one source, **79** have none. **79 is correct; 101 is wrong.** The same 101 is repeated in `docs/briefs/document-gap.md` §5 |

heading: 8. Conclusion
text:
| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is `pam/PAM` sufficient to derive the API under test? | ⛔ **No.** 3.7% strict, 27% on the most generous reading |
| Is it sufficient to derive request schemas? | ⛔ **No.** 3 validation attributes in 6,738 properties, none on a catalogue endpoint |
| Is it sufficient to derive response models or error codes? | ⛔ **No.** Neither exists in the snapshot |
| Should it be discarded? | ✅ **No** — keep it for C# types (2,674 properties), client call sites, and naming patterns (§3) |
| What *is* it? | A snapshot of the product that **consumes** the PAM API, plus supporting services. The API itself is hosted separately and is not in this tree |
| What would make it sufficient? | Swashbuckle/OpenAPI on the actual API host, plus model annotations or a DB schema dump. Costed in `data/analysis/solutions-A6A7.json` (`A6-*`) |

**One-line verdict:** the repository was provided to answer *"what is the API?"* and it answers a different
question — *"what does the product call?"* Both are useful; only one was asked for.

heading: Documentation Gap Analysis — what the PAM API documentation does not say
text:
**Subject:** `data/sources/PAM API (Internal Team).pdf` — 2,470 pages, Confluence export — plus the two
administrator guides (1,101 pp), assessed against the 1,306-endpoint catalogue and 1,868 executed calls.
**Verdict:** 🟡 The export is the **best payload source available and the only one worth investing in** —
and it cannot answer the one question validation depends on: *did this call succeed?*
**Headline:** **912 of 1,306 endpoints (69.8%) undocumented** · **3** error-code values in 2,470 pages ·
**0** pages stating an ordering constraint · **351 of 358** `ErrorCode` examples are `null`.
**Method:** static analysis only. **Zero HTTP requests, zero database queries.** Product docs were read
through the query layer (`tools/rag/query.py`), never by opening the corpus directly.
**Script:** `tools/measure_doc_gap.py` · **Row data:** `artifacts/analysis-data/doc-gap-coverage.json`
(one row per controller, 70 rows) · **Solutions:** `data/analysis/solutions-A6A7.json` (`A7-*`)
**Extends:** `docs/briefs/document-gap.md` and `docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` — §9 lists the
figures in those documents that this analysis corrects.

---

heading: 1. What was measured, and how
text:
One pass over `artifacts/rag-corpus/corpus.jsonl` (the page-cited extraction of the 2,470-page export),
compared against `APIConfig.java` and `tools/source-map.json`.

| Corpus measure | Value |
|---|---:|
| Pages scanned (`pam-api`) | **2,470** |
| Pages naming an `/api/<Controller>/<Action>` route | **1,051** |
| Pages naming only a bare action, no route | 191 |
| Pages naming a route **not in the catalogue** | 62 |
| Distinct routes cited anywhere in the document | **452** |
| JSON objects parsed | **3,194** |
| …bound to an endpoint by page proximity | **1,605** |
| …orphaned — no endpoint near enough to bind | **1,589** |
| JSON blocks that would not parse | 440 |

**Two definitions of "documented" are used deliberately**, because they answer different questions:

| Definition | Measure | Used for |
|---|---:|---|
| **Exact-route** — the literal `/api/<Controller>/<Action>` appears in the export | **394 / 1,306** | `endpoints_documented_confluence` in the JSON. Deterministic and page-citable |
| **Proximity-bound** — a JSON payload sits close enough to be attached to the endpoint | 424 / 1,306 | `payload_examples_available`. A hypothesis, not a contract |

⚠️ Proximity binding is the export's structural weakness, not a tooling choice: the document lists a route
as a heading and the payload beneath it, so **nearness is the only available signal**. Some bindings are
therefore wrong. Anything derived from the 1,605 bound payloads must be treated as a candidate.

---

heading: 2. Missing information — the four questions the documentation cannot answer
text:
| Question a tester must answer | Documented? | Measure |
|---|---|---:|
| What endpoints exist? | 🟡 Partially | 394 of 1,306 (30.2%) |
| What does a request body look like? | 🟡 Partially | 1,605 payloads, proximity-bound |
| **Which fields are mandatory?** | ⛔ **Not at all** | **0** — no field is marked mandatory anywhere |
| **What does a failure look like?** | ⛔ **Almost not at all** | **3** code values in 2,470 pages |
| **Which HTTP status means what?** | ⛔ **Not at all** | 104 incidental status mentions, no semantics |
| **In what order must calls be made?** | ⛔ **Not at all** | **0 of 2,470 pages** |
| Did a write persist? | ⛔ Not addressable | out of scope for documentation |

The mandatory-field row is the load-bearing one. It is absent from **every** source simultaneously — the
export marks nothing mandatory, and the product declares **3 `[Required]` attributes across 6,738
properties**, none of them on a catalogue endpoint (`A6-developer-repo-analysis.md` §4.1). Mandatory-ness
is currently *inferred* from "appears in every documented example": of 56 such inferred hints in the merged
map, **0 are backed by a declaration**, and only **1 of 217 create endpoints** has even one.

**Consequence for validation:** a generated create body is a guess. 204 of 217 creates fail, and the
failures are overwhelmingly `Validation error occurred - <Field> is Mandatory` and
`Could not convert string to integer` — requirements that exist only in server-side procedural code.

This is the most important coverage finding in the report, and it was not previously stated.

| Controller | Endpoints | Documented | In repo |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

**43% of the API surface has one documented endpoint between all of it.** These are not fringe controllers —

heading: 3.3 The catalogue is not a clean baseline either
text:
Documentation cannot be reconciled against a catalogue that itself contains defects. Measured:

| Anomaly | Count | Detail |
|---|---:|---|
| ⛔ Typo'd controller producing a hard 404 | 1 | `/api/Se0rviceDetailsV3/SetServiceSessionLogoutV2` — `APIConfig.java:893` *(supplied)* |
| ⛔ Double-slash typo hiding a real endpoint | 1 | `AzureKeyVault/GetDatabaseStatus` — `APIConfig.java:188` *(supplied)* |
| A version segment parsed as a controller | 3 | `/api/v1.0/GetConfig`, `/RegisterClient`, `/ClientAuth` — `APIConfig.java:496-498` |
| Unsubstituted `{placeholder}` in the declared path | **4** | `/api/Logs/GetAuditLog/{ID}`, `/api/User/{id}`, `/api/User/Details/{id}`, `/api/User/Delete/{id}` |
| Hardcoded environment-specific query strings | **7** | `?filname=5764`, `?LobId=2`, `?TicketId=LAMTest123`, plus 4 literal GUIDs |
| **Endpoints in the positive Excel absent from `APIConfig.java`** | **210** | mostly the SCIM `Service/*` and `User/*` surface *(supplied)* |
| Declared endpoints returning HTTP 404 live | **135** | `results.json` L1 |

`APIConfig.java` yields **1,308** distinct `Controller/Action` pairs; the two extras are the double-slash
`AzureKeyVault/GetDatabaseStatus` and the SCIM root `User/` (declared three times). **1,306 remains the
number to quote.**

**Consequence:** four artefacts disagree about what the API is — catalogue 1,306, documentation 452 routes,
Swagger 690 operations with ~6% name overlap *(prior)*, product snapshot 48 — and **none is authoritative**.
The 210 Excel-only endpoints mean even the test suite's own data files describe a surface the catalogue does
not declare.

heading: 4. Missing response models
text:
| What exists | What is absent |
|---|---|
| **159** envelope-shaped JSON examples (5.0% of the 3,194 parsed) | Any *declared* response schema. Not one endpoint has a typed response contract |
| **37 of 70** controllers have at least one response-shaped example | **33 of 70** have none at all |
| Response examples show the shape implicitly | No statement of which fields are always present, nullable, or typed how |

**How measured:** a documented JSON object counts as a response model if ≥2 of its keys are envelope keys
(`Program`, `Version`, `DateTime`, `Success`, `Message`, `Result`, `ErrorCode`, `ErrorMessage`, `aaData`,
`Output`). Recorded per controller as `response_model_documented`.

heading: ⛔ 31 shapes in reality, 6 of them documented
text:
**31 distinct response shapes** were measured across the 1,868 executed calls; only **6** match a shape the
documentation describes *(supplied)*. The export presents the envelope as though it were uniform.

Five shapes worth naming, because each defeats a different naive assertion:

| Shape | Defeats |
|---|---|
| `{Program, Version, DateTime, Success, Message, Result[]}` | — the assumed baseline |
| Same, but **no `Message`** field | any assertion that reads `Message` unconditionally |
| Same, but `Result` is an **object**, not an array | any assertion that indexes `Result[0]` |
| **Bare array**, no envelope at all | every envelope-based assertion |
| `{"Output": "1\|Parameter error occurred - …"}` | JSON-path assertions — the error is inside a pipe-delimited string |

**Consequence for validation:** no generated assertion may assume a fixed shape, so every check must be
shape-tolerant and probe defensively. This is exactly what the L3 `envelope` layer measures, and it failed
**590** times against 1,278 passes — the largest single failure class in the run after L4.

---

heading: 5. Missing error codes — the highest-value gap
text: This is where the documentation is weakest, and the previously reported figure was itself too generous.

heading: 5.1 What the 2,470 pages actually contain

heading: 5.2 ⚠️ Correcting the previously reported "4 documented error codes"
text:
`docs/briefs/document-gap.md` §2 and `docs/gaps/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` list **four** codes:
`203-SDC-GSDSI`, `203-SDC-GSDBSID`, `190-SSH`, `100-SSH`.

**Two of those four are false positives.** `190-SSH` and `100-SSH` are fragments of
`ServiceDisplayName` values — IP address followed by a hyphen and the service type:

```
pam-api:p1065   "ServiceDisplayName": "10.11.10.190@preeti:10.11.10.190-SSH LINUX"
pam-api:p1066   "ServiceDisplayName": "10.10.170.100@preeti:10.10.170.100-SSH LINUX"
```

A code-shaped regex matches `190-SSH` and `100-SSH` inside the final octet. A third such artefact,
`214-SSH`, appears at `pam-api:p1064` and was never reported. The fix is a negative lookbehind
(`(?<![\d.])`), documented at `measure_doc_gap.py:196`. Both prior documents also **miss** `APA:UR0021`.

**Corrected position: 3 documented code values, 2 in ARCON format, against 108 observed live — not 4.**
The gap is wider than previously stated, and 98% of documented examples show `ErrorCode: null`.

heading: 5.3 Status-code semantics
text:
| Status | Mentions across 2,470 pages |
|---|---:|
| 200 | 46 |
| 400 | 21 |
| 401 | 12 |
| 500 | 11 |
| 201 | 5 |
| 404 · 503 | 3 each |
| 403 | 2 |
| 405 | 1 |

**104 incidental mentions in 2,470 pages**, and nowhere a statement of what any status *means* for this API.

**Consequence for validation — the decisive one:** this API signals failure in the response **body** at HTTP
200. Without a code register and without status semantics, a rejected request is indistinguishable from an
accepted one. Measured: L4 `message-semantics` failed **458** times; **289 of 1,868 calls returned HTTP 200
with `Success: false`** *(prior)*; and `0` of 3,317 existing negative test rows carry an `ExpectedErrorCode`,
because there is no documented value to assert.

heading: 6. Missing examples
text:
The export's real strength, and its three consumability defects.

| What exists | Measure |
|---|---:|
| Parseable JSON examples | **3,194** |
| …bound to an endpoint | **1,605** |
| …orphaned | **1,589** |

available. Three problems stop it being consumed automatically:

|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **Payloads are not bound to their endpoint** — binding is by page proximity | 1,589 of 3,194 orphaned (49.7%) | A parser cannot reliably tell which body belongs to which route. Every binding is a hypothesis |
| 2 | ⛔ **Mandatory vs optional is never marked** | 0 fields marked | The direct cause of 204 of 217 creates failing |
| 3 | **No field types, lengths, formats or patterns** | 0 constraints | Cannot distinguish an id from free text; cannot generate a boundary case |

heading: 7. Missing workflows
text:
| What exists | What is absent |
|---|---|
| Endpoints documented individually, page by page | ⛔ **Any statement of ordering, dependency or prerequisite** |

**How measured:** all 2,470 `pam-api` pages were scanned for ordering language — `must first`,
`before calling`, `before you`, `after creating`, `prerequisite`, `in the following order`, `step 1`,
`first call`, `depends on the`, `returned by the previous`, `obtained from the`, and six further variants.

> ⛔ **Result: 0 of 2,470 pages contain any ordering or prerequisite phrase.**

Nor is the producer→consumer relationship implicit: **1,680** chain candidates were derived, every one by
**field-name matching**, and **0 of 1,680** came from documentation or an observed producer response *(prior)*.

**Consequence for validation — this is the root of the chaining failure.** Because no dependency is
declared, the harness must guess that the `ServiceId` returned by one endpoint is the `ServiceId` another
consumes. When the producing create fails, the guess cannot be tested at all:

| Layer | Result |
|---|---|
| L5 `chain-key-extracted` | 982 pass · ⛔ **196 fail — every one `resolved []; MISSING ['NEW_ID']`** |
| L6 `record-exists` | ⛔ **2 pass · 105 fail** of 107 attempted |
| Flow verdicts | 30 PASS · **296 FAIL** of 326 |

The mechanism itself is sound — one chain was proven to **5 hops** with no hardcoded values *(prior)*. What
is missing is the declaration of which endpoint feeds which.
