| D8 | 2026-08-03 | Instruction loading is **import + `UserPromptSubmit` hook**, so mid-session edits apply immediately |
| D9 | 2026-08-03 | **`BLAST/Objective.md` stays the active instruction file.** No new file — the existing one gains the auto-load. Its permanent counterpart is `objective_original_origin.md` at the workspace root |
| D10 | 2026-08-03 | `Objective.md` holds **active instruction only**. Historical content lives here and is never copied back |
| D11 | 2026-08-03 | **`pending-tasks-in-queue.md` retired.** No separate backlog file — see §6 for its final contents |
| D12 | 2026-08-03 | **Standard CLI workflow adopted** — record the instruction in `Objective.md` *before* implementing; ask ambiguities as MCQ; append outcomes here. Written into `CLAUDE.md` §Standard workflow |
| D13 | 2026-08-03 | Step 2 fires on **substantive task requests only** — not questions, conversational replies, or process changes. A correction **amends** the current instruction rather than replacing it |
| D14 | 2026-08-03 | On overwrite, the outgoing objective is **always appended here first** — including objectives superseded before any work was done |
| D15 | — | **Objective Register adopted** (§0). Every archived objective carries ten mandatory fields under a sequential `OBJ-NNN` ID. Enforced by `CLAUDE.md` §Objective lifecycle |
| D16 | — | **No dates in objective records.** The sequential ID is the ordering. **Filesystem paths are exempt** — run folders are identifiers, and stripping them would break the traceability the register exists for |
| D17 | — | The no-dates rule applies **going forward only**. The existing dated log (§4) and decisions D1–D14 stay as written, honouring append-only. Register backfilled as OBJ-001 … OBJ-006 |
| D18 | — | **`CLAUDE.md` split into path-scoped rules.** Detail that applies to one area moved to `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` frontmatter, loading on demand. Root file cut 523 → 387 lines. **Safety rules stay unconditional** — a rule that only loads after you open a matching file is useless for preventing the first destructive call |
| D19 | — | **Large-file protocol adopted** (`CLAUDE.md` §Large files). Any file over ~1,500 lines is treated as truncated until proven otherwise; files with a query layer are never read directly. This archive split into an index + `objective-history/NN-*.md`, verified lossless. **`§N` is the stable citation scheme** — files may be reorganised, references never break |
| D20 | — | **`AGENTS.md` now auto-loads.** Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, never `AGENTS.md`, so the repo's 210-line reference was invisible while a 9-line boilerplate file loaded in its place — one line of which pointed at a path that has never existed. Fixed by `@AGENTS.md` in `pam_automation_bootstrap/CLAUDE.md`. `.claude/rules/automation-repo.md` slimmed to the delta `AGENTS.md` omits (the `rowIndex` race, the `Playwright.create()` leak, the RestAssured warning) |
| D21 | — | **Execution is scheduled separately from derivation.** `OBJ-016` refreshes everything *derived* every morning; `OBJ-017` executes the suite **Sundays 10:00**. The split exists because fresh source code changes no KPI — only an execution does — so "pull daily" and "execute daily" are different decisions with very different costs |
| D22 | — | **Authored analysis is pinned to the run it was measured in.** N and N-1 are now resolved at run time, so a new execution becomes current automatically — but the benchmark narrative, the overall-trend line and the three headline findings (1,022 false passes · 19 endpoints accepting an invalid token · 85 min lost) were written about **one** run. When N moves they are **withheld, not reattached**: reattaching them would assert measurements the new run never produced |
| D23 | — | **The weekly execution is bounded, and retried exactly once.** Full suite inside a 6-hour `--budget-seconds` wall clock; a run that aborts gets **one** `--resume`, then stops, keeps the partial run and flags it incomplete rather than promoting it to current. An unattended retry loop against an environment that lost 85 of 329 minutes to app-pool downtime is how a small problem becomes a large one |
| D24 | — | **⚠️ The "no scheduled token generation" rule is deliberately relaxed — for the weekly job only.** A weekly run cannot avoid generating a token: the cache lives 24 h and the gap is 7 days, so it is always expired at 10:00. `token_guard.py`'s own docstring says *"never add … a scheduled/cron token refresh"*, and `ISSUE-009`'s lockout hit `GenericScheduler`, which is also the data-warehouse ETL service account. The owner chose to relax it with three mitigations that make it materially safer than what caused the lockout: **(1)** the environment is probed **unauthenticated and first**, so a token is never spent against a host that cannot answer; **(2)** exactly **one** attempt, through `token_guard`, never a retry or backoff; **(3)** a failure **latches permanently**, blocking every future run until a human clears it — so failures cannot accumulate, and accumulation rather than a single attempt is what tripped the lockout. ⛔ The rule stands everywhere else, and `token_guard.py` itself must never gain a scheduled refresh |
| D25 | — | **The development branch is `Dev`, from now onwards.** Supersedes the standing "develop on `AI`" rule set in `workbench/archive/approach/instruction.md` item 8. Measured basis: `AI` holds **no unique commits** (`git rev-list --left-right --count AI...Dev` = `0 2`), so it had become a stale point on `Dev` rather than a working branch; and the PAM submodule gitlink tracks `Dev`, so a fix landing on `AI` could never reach the submodule pointer. ⛔ **The never-push / never-merge rule is unchanged** — work is committed on `Dev` locally and the owner takes it from there. Local `Dev` was 3 commits behind `origin/Dev` when this was set; the owner pulls |
| D26 | — | **Maven execution is permitted for dependency remediation.** A named exception to the `OBJ-010` rule that "execute everything" means the dynamic framework in `workbench/scripts/`, never the bootstrap suite. The exception is narrow and justified: a `pom.xml` change can only be validated by resolving and compiling against the real dependency graph, which no Python harness can do. Covers `dependency:tree`, `test-compile`, and targeted suite runs for Excel / DB / Playwright / API regression. ⛔ The `ActivityLogs` blocklist (`GetErrorLogs`, `GetLogs`, `GetAllActiveUserDetails` stop the IIS app pool) and the one-token-attempt rule still bind |
| D27 | — | **Full remediation, not the minimum-risk subset.** The owner chose all fourteen dependency actions over the three zero-risk ones (jxl→log4j exclusion, remove `org.json`, remove `mysql-connector-j`) that alone would have cleared 3 CRITICAL and 5 HIGH. Rationale: the developer had **already** chosen and accepted five of the six target versions in `pam` commit `0520b6b79`, and bootstrap commit `e278fd399` reverted them — so remediating the source of truth fully is what stops the next hand-copy from re-importing the old versions. One correction to the developer's own choice was required: `jackson-databind` **2.22.0** is still vulnerable (GHSA-5gvw-p9qm-jgwh, GHSA-5jmj-h7xm-6q6v), so **2.22.2** is used |

---
| D28 | — | **Push rights now differ per repository — the uniform "never push" rule is superseded.** Three repositories are in play and each has its own rights: **`dynamic-api-validator`** (the workspace root, `OBJ-024`) is **pull + push**, the owner having created it and granted approval; **PAM Bootstrap Automation** (`Automation gitlab repo/pam_automation_bootstrap/`) and **PAM** (`pam/`) are **pull only, never push**. Pulling from the two nested repos is now explicitly permitted and is the supported way to pick up upstream code — previously the guidance was silent on it, which had been read as prohibition. ⛔ The never-push half is unchanged for both nested repos, and the bootstrap release path still runs owner-reviews → owner-pushes → owner-bumps-the-gitlink. Enforcement note: `.claude/settings.json` carries the deny rules, **the assistant is blocked from editing that file** (the classifier refuses to let an agent widen its own permissions — correctly), so a denied push is fixed by an owner edit and never by a workaround. Two mechanical limits worth knowing: `deny` beats `allow`, and rules match **command text, not the target repository**, so cwd must be confirmed before any push. ✅ **Enforced mechanically** as well as by instruction: both nested repos carry `remote.origin.pushurl = DISABLED-push-blocked-per-D28` in local `.git/config`, so a push from either fails before reaching the network, for any caller. Fetch URLs untouched — both remotes verified still reachable and both trees clean after the change |
| D29 | — | **`OBJ-023` is closed without resuming, and reproducibility moves onto the scheduled path.** The owner put the paused API re-execution on hold and instructed that it be marked completed rather than resumed manually: the standing `PAM-Weekly-API-Execution` trigger runs every Sunday at 10:00 and covers the next full execution automatically. Measured basis for why this is the safer choice, not merely the cheaper one: resuming the remaining 569 flows required a **fresh `/arcontoken` call** on `GenericScheduler` — a shared functional account that also serves the data-warehouse ETL and has locked twice recently — because the pinned token's 24 h lifetime elapsed during the pause. `D24` grants scheduled token generation **only** to the weekly job, and only because of three mitigations (unauthenticated host probe first, exactly one attempt, permanent latch on failure). A manual resume would have taken the same risk with none of them. ⛔ The partial run `Reports/Runs/2026-08-19_133400/` (178 of 747 flows) is **retained as evidence and never promoted to N** — it is not a suite result. `obj023_reproducibility.py` stays built and self-tested, awaiting the scheduled run as its second data set |
| D30 | — | **`engage` may fast-forward both nested repos when their trees are clean — this resolves a live contradiction in `CLAUDE.md`.** Two rules disagreed: `D28` and §Edit scope grant **Pull ✅** on `pam/` and the bootstrap repo, while §Edit scope's *Committing on `Dev`* paragraph said *"Do **not** pull to fix it — merging is the owner's call."* The owner chose the permissive reading, bounded: a pull is `--ff-only` and is attempted **only** when the working tree is clean, an upstream exists, the branch is strictly behind (never diverged), and no merge or rebase is in progress. Measured basis for why this is safe rather than merely convenient: `--ff-only` cannot create a merge commit and cannot run at all against a dirty tree, so it has no path to overwriting uncommitted work — the risk the original wording was written to prevent. ⛔ Unchanged: **push** rights stay per-repository (`D28`) and both nested repos keep their `pushurl` block; `engage` never merges, rebases, resets, stashes, cleans or resolves a conflict, and a **diverged** branch is always reported for a human decision rather than reconciled. The old *do-not-pull* sentence is superseded for the fast-forward case only; the release path (owner reviews → owner pushes → owner bumps the gitlink) is untouched |
| D31 | — | **`engage` is safe-by-default rather than deny-by-default — a deliberate, narrow departure from the harness convention.** Every other script in `workbench/scripts/` requires `--execute` because it runs unattended and can issue HTTP to a shared environment. `engage` is human-invoked, issues **zero product HTTP**, and its only state changes are `git fetch` and a guarded `--ff-only` pull, both non-destructive by construction. Requiring `--execute` would defeat the entire point — one word in, ready workspace out. `--dry-run` is provided for inspection. ⛔ The deny-by-default rule is unchanged for every other script, and `engage` never relaxes it on their behalf: when it triggers `obj016_daily_refresh.py` it passes that script's own `--execute` flag, and it will not invoke `obj017_weekly_execution.py`, `chain_runner.py` or `token_guard refresh` under any circumstances |
| D32 | — | **The missed `2026-08-23` weekly API execution is deliberately not made up; the next execution is the scheduled `2026-08-30` occurrence.** Owner instruction, given after `engage` surfaced the gap. **No scheduler change was required to honour it** — measured at the time of the decision, `PAM-Weekly-API-Execution` is `State: Ready`, its trigger is enabled (weekly, Sundays 10:00, `StartBoundary 2026-08-12T10:00:00+05:30`), `NumberOfMissedRuns: 1`, and `NextRunTime` is already `2026-08-30 10:00`. The missed occurrence is not queued for catch-up, so the correct action was to change nothing and start nothing. ⛔ **This decision sets *when*, not *whether the job works*.** The task's last actual attempt was `2026-08-16 10:00`, which **exited 1 after 0.2 min** against run `2026-08-16_100005`; its `workbench/.weekly/last-run.json` does not show this, because that file records a successful **dry run** from 2026-08-19 and so reads healthy while the schedule is not. Nothing about waiting for 2026-08-30 addresses the exit-1 cause: if it is still present, that occurrence fails the same way and the reproducibility assessment behind `D29` goes unmet for a third consecutive week. Diagnosing the exit 1 is therefore still open work, and is independent of this decision |
| D33 | — | **`OBJ-025` target structure signed off: `Standard Four` — `docs/` `data/` `tools/` `artifacts/` `state/`, plus root-pinned `CLAUDE.md` / `README.md` / `.claude/` / `BLAST/` and the two immovable nested checkouts. 21 top-level entries -> 13.** Chosen from three candidate architectures scored by three independent judging lenses: breakage risk, fidelity to the owner's brief, and one-year maintainability. Aggregate 22.5 / 18.0 / 17.0. The runner-up `Loop-Aligned` was rejected on three measured fatal flaws -- case-only renames that silently no-op under `core.ignorecase = true`, splitting two append-only archive files, and relocating `BLAST/Objective.md` whose path is an absolute literal in a hook the assistant cannot edit. `Frozen Core` scored highest on safety (9/10) but 4/10 against the brief, and created its own defect: a top-level `Reports/` beside `docs/reports/`. An adversarial completeness critic returned **needs-revision on all three**, and its nine required additions are folded into the executed plan -- notably the blocking sign-off gate itself, a `pre-obj025` rollback tag (v0.2 is nine commits back and is *not* the pre-restructure state), a gitignored-file manifest before and after every move, and explicit `dist/` handling. |
| D34 | — | **Phase 0 hardens before anything moves — the sequencing decision that makes the rest survivable.** The restructure's cost was measured as **103 path bindings, 75 of which break silently**, not as the cost of moving files (git history is 9 commits, 530.86 MB packs to 23.27 MiB, and `git mv` on a directory is one operation regardless of the 14,035 files inside it). Two idioms produced the silence: **18 sites counted parent directories** in four different spellings -- `parents[2]`, `.parent.parent`, `os.path.join(HERE,'..','..')`, `$PSScriptRoot '..\..'` -- so a grep for `parents[` found only ten of them; and **7 sites searched upward for a directory containing both `Reports/` and `Automation gitlab repo/`**, which made two *content* folder names part of the executable interface, with three of the seven being inline copies invisible to a grep for the function name. Both are now replaced by one marker-based `workspace_root()` in `paths.py`, keyed on `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/` -- the two entries the harness pins to the root and which no restructure may rename. ⛔ Do not reintroduce a depth count. The decisive precedent: the **2026-07-29** `Reports/` reorganisation broke `Graphify/api-graph/build_api_graph.py:51-52`, which still points at `Reports/Issues/Evidence/legacy-qa_mssql` -- a directory absent for four weeks, failing silently, unnoticed. |
| D35 | — | **Three owner rulings at the sign-off gate.** (1) The `.claude/settings.json` `SessionStart` hook holds an absolute literal to `obj013_loop.py`; the assistant is blocked from editing that file by design, so step 9 stops and hands the owner a one-line edit. `BLAST/Objective.md` is deliberately left in place so the `UserPromptSubmit` hook needs **no** edit -- one owner action, not two. (2) `Automation gitlab repo/graphify-out.local-backup-OBJ007/` -- 153 MB / 1,092 files belonging to no git repository, inside the immovable gitignored tree -- is **left untouched**, and stays flagged as undecided. (3) Only **two of three** space-bearing directory names can be eliminated: `Company Documents/` and `Developer Repository Issues/` both go, while `Automation gitlab repo/` is immovable under `D28`. The objective's own text asked for three; the contradiction was surfaced at the gate rather than quietly delivering two and calling it three. Also confirmed: `required-context/` folds into `docs/gaps/` (it is not paired with `Reports/`), and the target tag is **`v0.3`** -- `v0.2` is the current tagged state, not the goal. |
| D36 | — | **The DevProjects Control Center is a decision interface, never a security boundary, and its server extends `D31`'s safe-by-default reasoning rather than widening it.** The owner chose the local-server execution model over a static handoff so one button executes approved actions. That creates a listening process, so the posture is stated rather than assumed: **the browser never sends a command.** It sends an action *type* plus a target, both looked up in a server-side `ACTIONS` table; there is no code path from request data to a shell string. Three action types exist — `repo.pull_ff_only`, `data.refresh`, `decision.note` — and anything else is refused **by name**, producing an audit line rather than a silent no-op. Absent on purpose and staying absent: push, merge, rebase, reset, checkout, clean, stash, conflict resolution, credential edits, deletion, and anything issuing product HTTP (the server has no HTTP client at all). Every git action still goes through `engage_core.run_git`'s allow-list and `policy_for`'s per-repository rights (`D28`), so the UI cannot widen either: **if the CLI would refuse it, so does this.** The server also **re-derives each plan at execute time** instead of trusting what the page displayed, because a stale “safe to pull” is exactly how uncommitted work gets overwritten. Bound to `127.0.0.1` only (verified with `netstat`), with a random per-process token held in memory and never written to disk. ⛔ **`always_approve` is granted only to an action type declared both reversible and safe**, refused otherwise — a potentially destructive operation must never become silently automatic. ⛔ **Do not widen the whitelist to make the UI more capable.** If an action is not safe enough for `engage`, it is not safe enough here; this server is downstream of that decision, not a route around it. Verified end-to-end against a running server: empty and wrong tokens both return 403, a forged `repo.push` is refused by name and executes nothing, and `always_approve` on it is refused at decide time. |
| D37 | — | **`not_interested` expires by itself: suppression is keyed to a state fingerprint, not to the item.** The owner's requirement was explicit — *avoid permanently hiding important issues merely because they were previously ignored.* Every decidable item therefore carries a fingerprint of its material state, and a recorded suppression only matches while that fingerprint matches. The moment the underlying facts move the item reappears, flagged **reappeared** rather than surfacing as if new, so a reader knows a prior dismissal lapsed rather than never existing. This deliberately reuses the drift loop's waiver mechanism, where a waiver is keyed to the `evidence_hash` it was granted against and expires when the measurement moves — one idea applied twice rather than two half-solutions. `ignore_once` is scoped to the run it was made in and cannot outlive it. Both journals (`state/control-center/decisions.jsonl`, `executions.jsonl`) are **append-only**, so a decision history cannot be quietly rewritten, and both are tracked: like `state/daily/`, they are the only evidence a choice was made. |
| D38 | — | **Defect population is the Bug / Security Fix / Client-Support / Performance subset, and `Duplicate`-status tickets are held out of it.** On the original HF12/HF13 scope that is 55 of 82 client tickets, not 82: Story (13), Task (9) and Sub-task (3) are client-raised work but are not defects, and counting them in a defect rate understates module quality. A `Duplicate` is the same defect twice, so leaving it in inflates every module percentage. Non-defects are still reported — separately, with their own count. |
| D39 | — | **Linked and parent tickets outside a scope window are evidence, never population.** Measured on the first scope: 61 of 68 link edges and **all 58** parent references pointed outside HF12+HF13, one into a different project entirely (`MP-533`). A hard two-version fence would therefore have made recurrence structurally invisible, while pulling the linked closure into the population would have moved every denominator. Clone/parent/blocks edges are followed read-only and cited as evidence; percentages stay on the in-scope population. |
| D40 | — | **No new top-level folder — the analysis lands in the existing five drawers.** The owner's sketch proposed a root-level `client-ticket-analysis/`; `OBJ-025` had just reduced 21 top-level entries to 12 and set the rule that the next objective must have an obvious home without growing another. Placement: `tools/jira/` (executable) · `docs/analysis/` (reports and the dated `summary/` series) · `artifacts/client-tickets/` (generated data) · `state/client-analysis/` (job evidence). |
| D41 | — | **Daily at 09:00, as a registered Windows task — `PAM-Client-Ticket-Analysis`.** Originally agreed as manual-first, then the owner extended the objective to a scheduled daily activity. It is the third scheduled task in this workspace and the only one that touches Jira. It is read-only by construction, issues **zero** product HTTP, and never touches git. Dated summaries (`summary_<date>.md`) are never overwritten across days; a same-day re-run replaces only that day's file. ⚠️ Its first registration **exited 1 in under a second and wrote nothing** — `set PYTHONUTF8=1 && ...` captures the trailing space, so Python refused to start on an invalid `PYTHONUTF8` value. Quoting the assignment (`set "PYTHONUTF8=1"`) fixed it and the task was re-fired to exit 0 before being declared done. **Do not trust a registered task until it has been fired once and its own log has grown.** |
| D42 | — | **The build-wise axis is `Affected Milestone` (`customfield_10092`), not `Fix versions` and not `Milestone`.** Owner instruction, given as a question about which field the analysis used and answered by measurement. The two fields answer different questions: `Affected Milestone` is the build the **client was running** when they hit the defect, `fixVersions` is the release the **fix ships in**. A hotfix accumulates fixes for defects found on earlier builds, so a `fixVersion`-keyed build line reports *release content* and was being read as *build quality*. Measured on the same 20 `35.8.29` versions: **1,384** client tickets by `fixVersion` against **2,010** by `Affected Milestone`; **1,369** tickets carry an Affected Milestone and *no fix version at all*, structurally invisible to the old query, against **38** the other way; the heaviest build moves from `base` (262) to `HF6` (399) and `HF1` (388), with `base` only **69**; and the current build `HF13` falls from an apparent **27** client tickets to **2**, because the 27 were fixes *scheduled into* HF13. ⛔ **Root cause of the original error, recorded so it cannot recur:** the previous revision checked the **native** `affectedVersion` field, measured it at 0% project-wide, concluded that *no field records the build a client was on*, and recovered the fact from build tokens clients had typed into ticket titles — a fallback that fired on **9** tickets while `customfield_10092` carried the same fact as a structured field on **97.3%** of the population. Finding a native field empty is not evidence that the fact is unrecorded. ⚠️ **Three fields in this Jira instance are named `Affected Milestone`-something and two of them are 0% on PAMIT** (`cf 10214`, `cf 10219`), so selecting one returns an **empty build line that reads as a clean result rather than a wrong query**; the field name also carries a trailing period (`Affected Milestone.`), which is why the JQL uses `cf[10092]` rather than the name. ⛔ **`Milestone` is not a usable axis in PAMIT**: `Release Milestone.` (`cf 10100`) is 9% and legacy with unrelated old lines as singleton values, `Forward Merge Milestone` (`cf 10238`) is 63% populated but **344 of 388 values are the literal string `None`** — population without information — and `Release Milestone`, `PAM_Release Milestone`, `CI_Release_Milestone` and the native `Affects versions` are all 0%. All ten are recorded in `D1` §0.2 and on workbook sheet `10 Field Audit` so the measurement is not repeated. **Attribution rules:** a multiselect ticket is attributed to the **earliest** in-family build it names (a defect reported against both HF5 and HF9 escaped from HF5; crediting HF9 would blame the later build for an inherited defect and understate the escape gap); out-of-family values are reported, never dropped; and per-build counts therefore sum **above** the ticket total, so the de-duplicated total is the population figure. `fixVersions` is retained as the second axis of escape latency only. |
| D43 | — | **No count without its tickets — every reported figure must be traceable to the individual JIRA tickets behind it.** Owner instruction, stated as *"if the analysis says Environment – 104 tickets then I want all 104 ticket numbers"*. A total, a percentage, a summary or an aggregate is not an answer on its own. Enforced in four places rather than promised: **(1)** workbook sheet `04 Ticket Details` carries one row per ticket in the union of every counted pool, with each pool and each testing area as a Yes/No column, so **filtering the sheet reproduces any reported figure exactly** — the count becomes a view over the data rather than a separate assertion; **(2)** sheet `09 Count Reconciliation` restates every headline count as a **live `COUNTIFS` over sheet 04**, beside the value the analysis computed, beside a `PASS`/`FAIL` comparison, and Excel recomputes it on open, so the reader verifies the totals **without trusting the generator** — a number the generator both computes and prints proves nothing, since both come from the same code; **(3)** `pamit_workbook.verify()` reconciles every pool count and every area count against the ticket universe *before* the workbook is declared good and **exits non-zero on any mismatch**, so an unreproducible figure fails the build instead of shipping; **(4)** every testing-area row carries **all** its member keys rather than a sample of six. ⚠️ **Two places where counts legitimately do not add up, and both must be stated wherever the figure appears:** per-build counts sum above the ticket total because `Affected Milestone` is a multiselect and 55 tickets name two in-family builds; and testing-area counts sum past 100% because the area axis is multi-label — a defect that is both a boundary failure and a compatibility failure is a gap in **both** kinds of testing and is counted in both. Verified at delivery: 693 weak-spot rows equal the sum of the 15 area counts with zero per-area mismatch, the four pool columns reproduce 2,010 / 190 / 401 / 171 exactly, and no weak-spot ticket is absent from the source sheet. |
| D44 | — | **One consolidated Excel workbook; a new analysis area is a new worksheet in it, never a new `.xlsx`.** Owner instruction, given with the standing extension that later requirements reuse the same workbook *"unless there is a strong technical reason not to"*. The one output path is `artifacts/workbooks/PAM-Client-Ticket-Analysis.xlsx`, and adding an analysis means adding a `sheet_*` builder to `build()` in `tools/jira/pamit_workbook.py` plus a matching row to the manifest in `sheet_readme()`. ⚠️ Those two are hand-kept in step: add a builder and forget the manifest row, and sheet `00 README` describes a workbook that is not the one on disk. Delivered with **11 worksheets** — README, Testing Weak Spots (ticket level), Weak Spot Summary, Test Scenario Gaps, Ticket Details, Build-wise, Escape Latency, Regression Signal, Module & Category, Count Reconciliation, Field Audit. ⛔ Two Excel limits are handled structurally in `_cell()` because both corrupt a sheet **silently**: a cell holds at most 32,767 characters and an over-length write produces a file Excel *repairs* on open by discarding the whole sheet, and a value beginning `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is parsed as a formula — PAM ticket summaries do start with `-`, and the result is `#NAME?` where the title should be. Verified at delivery: zero cells over the limit. |
| D45 | — | **The master Excel workbook is refreshed as part of the daily run, in place — never as a new file, and never as a second scheduled task.** Owner requirement (`OBJ-029` #8), extending `D44` from "one workbook" to "one workbook, refreshed daily". Implementation: the workbook build lives **inside `pamit_client_analysis.py`**, after the report is written, so the existing `PAM-Client-Ticket-Analysis` task (09:00 daily) refreshes it with **no change to the task registration** at all. ⛔ **Deliberately not a second task**: two tasks can fire at different times and leave the workbook describing yesterday's analysis while the report describes today's — one process cannot drift from itself. ⚠️ **A workbook failure must never fail the analysis.** The report, the dated summary, the snapshot and the CSVs are written *first* and are the primary deliverable; the likeliest failure is the file being open in Excel, which is a desk-level problem, not an analysis problem, so it is caught, reported loudly with the rebuild command, and the exit code is left unchanged. `--no-workbook` skips it for a report-only run. **History across refreshes**: the workbook is overwritten daily, so history cannot live in its sheets. It lives in the retained dated snapshots under `artifacts/client-tickets/snapshots/`, which are never deleted, and sheet `12 Daily History` is a **derived view** over them with day-over-day deltas. ⛔ Derived, not appended: an appended sheet would be lost the first time the workbook was rebuilt from scratch and could silently disagree with the snapshots. A break in the date sequence means the job did not run that day, and the gap is shown rather than smoothed over — the 2026-08-30 gap is visible, and the basis change from `fixVersion` to `Affected Milestone` is labelled per row so pre- and post-`D42` figures are never read as a trend. |
| D46 | — | **Use every regression-related field Jira actually holds, and mark an unavailable fact `Info not available in JIRA` rather than leaving it blank or inferring it.** Owner requirement (`OBJ-029` #9). A 276-field sweep found **22 regression-shaped fields**, of which 15 carry data. ⛔ **The sweep found a second instance of the exact error class behind `D42`, and it was larger.** §13 of the report claimed *"`Module`, `Category`, `Sub-Category`, `Root Cause` … all unpopulated (0 / 376). The whole taxonomy is derived from ticket text. Jira holds no categorisation to cross-check it against."* That measured `customfield_10113` (*Root Cause*, **0.2%**) and `customfield_10199` (*Root cause*, **0.1%**) — two decoy fields — and never measured **`customfield_10245` (*RCA*), which is 80.7% populated (1,622 / 2,010)** with a structured taxonomy of **33 values in 15 families**. It is the most populated analytical field in the project and it had never been used. `RCA Details (Impact Analysis)` (`cf 10567`) sits alongside it at **79.2%**. **The lesson, now recorded twice: in this Jira instance several fields share a concept and only one is live — measure every same-named candidate before concluding a fact is unrecorded.** Two findings the RCA field makes possible: **315 tickets are classified by the product team as not a product defect** (`Requests - Enhancement`, `Requests - Information Request`, `Requests - APEM Tool`, `Requests - Script Request`, `Others - Working as expected`, `Not a bug`, `Miscommunication`), so a testing weak spot attributed to one of them is a **false finding** — ⚠️ reported, never silently applied, because re-cutting a denominator on a field that is 19% empty would be a worse error than the one it fixes, and the defect population stays keyed on issue type (`D38`); and **a set of tickets name a testing or analysis failure as the root cause** (`Analysis - Inadequate Test Coverage`, `Insufficient Unit Test case`, `Analysis - Incomplete Requirement`, `Analysis - Inadequate Technical Design`, `Environment - Non replicated`) which is the **strongest evidence in the whole analysis for a testing gap**, because the product team recorded the cause rather than the report inferring it. Also brought in: `Fixed Date` (51.0%), `Reopen RCA` (7.3% — Code Fix 48, Dependency failure 29, Audit 23, Hosting Issue 22, Tester Understanding 17, Data Issue 8), `Reopen RCA details` (7.6%), `Reopen Original Ticket ID` (7.1%), `ReOpen Date` (4.1%), `ReOpen Time Spent` (3.6%), `RCA Category updated?` and `RCA Review Remarks` (1.2% each). ⛔ **Fields that exist but are never populated, so any value derived from them would be invented:** `Phase` (`cf 10164`, 0%) and `ReopenCount` (`cf 11018`, 0%). **Defect-injection phase is therefore not answerable**, and the temptation to derive it from the RCA family is refused explicitly: `Code - Logic Issue` records where a defect was *found in code*, not the phase in which it was *introduced*, and mapping one to the other would produce a phase-containment metric that reads as measured and would drive real test-strategy decisions. Also unavailable: regression-test-executed / suite name, requirement or user-story link, and detected-by stage — no such field exists. ⚠️ **Sentinel discipline**: `Info not available in JIRA` is used verbatim and covers three distinct situations a blank cell would have flattened into one — the field does not exist, the field exists but is never populated, or the field is empty on that ticket. An unavailable field gets an **explicit workbook column reading the sentinel all the way down**, because a *missing* column reads as "not analysed". ⚠️ **Field-specific sentinels are needed**: `Reopen Original Ticket ID` is free text and 64 of its 142 values are junk answers ("No", "NONE", "na"), which would invent ticket links — but "No" cannot go in the global sentinel set, because it is a legitimate value for every Yes/No select in the project including `Is reopen from customer`. |
| D47 | — | **Manual push is permitted to the PAM Bootstrap Automation repository; automatic push is not. `pam/` is unchanged and stays blocked.** Owner instruction, given as a single scoped amendment to `D28`: keep pull enabled for all three repositories, keep automatic push for the workspace repo, **enable manual push for `pam_automation_bootstrap`**, and keep push blocked for `pam`. The rights table is therefore no longer two-valued — it is **pull / automatic push / manual push** across three repositories, and the two push columns must never be collapsed back into one. Asked who may perform the manual push, the owner chose: **the assistant may push, on an explicit per-push instruction in that turn** — never on its own initiative, never as the closing step of a task, never scheduled. ⛔ **The failure mode this rule exists to prevent, recorded because it is the obvious one:** *"the task is done and there are unpushed commits"* is **not** an instruction to push. Commit on `Dev` and say so. **Mechanism:** `remote.origin.pushurl = DISABLED-push-blocked-per-D28` was removed from the bootstrap repo's **local** `.git/config` with `git config --unset remote.origin.pushurl`; `pam` keeps its block and it was re-measured as present immediately afterwards. Reverse with `git -C <repo> config remote.origin.pushurl DISABLED-push-blocked-per-D28`. ✅ **Why this is safe, and the measurement that makes it so:** the pushurl was never what stopped *automatic* pushes. `push` is in `obj016_daily_refresh.FORBIDDEN` and absent from `engage_core.ALLOWED`, so no scheduled task, harness script, `engage` run or Control Center action can emit a `git push` for **any** repository — including the workspace one, which has no pushurl block at all. Removing a pushurl does not touch that ban; it sits upstream of it. `engage_selftest.py` asserts it directly (`guard: git push refused`) and ran **57 passed, 0 failed** after the change. So "automatic push ⛔ / manual push ✅" needed **no new mechanism** — only the removal of the blanket block. **Encoded, not just documented:** `engage_core.Policy` gained a second field so the distinction survives in code — `push` (may this repo be pushed at all) and `push_auto` (may it be pushed without being asked), with a module-level assertion that no policy grants `push_auto` without `push`. Flattening them back to one boolean would silently re-grant automatic push to the bootstrap repo, which is precisely what this decision withholds. `classify()` and `engage.recommend()` now say *"manual push only, on an explicit instruction"* rather than *"ready to push"* for that repo. **Verified at delivery:** bootstrap fetch URL untouched and `ls-remote` resolves (`refs/heads/Dev` at `7d34e1c`, still the only remote branch — there is no `origin/AI`), local `Dev` equals `origin/Dev` at `7d34e1c`, tree clean, and **nothing was pushed as part of making this change**. ⚠️ **`.claude/settings.json` was deliberately left untouched.** It carries no push rule at all — only `git merge` and `git remote set-url` denies — the assistant cannot edit it by design, and the owner scoped this change to push rights. Documentation sites updated: root `CLAUDE.md` (rights table, release path, BLAST precedence row, `/go-go-go` note) and root `README.md` (drawer table, release-path diagram, branch section). ⛔ **`merge` is unchanged and still never the assistant's, in any of the three repositories.** |

heading: 2026-07-28 — BLAST Run 1: the premise was checked, and it was false
text:
**Instructed:** first formal objective — dynamic API validation script generation. The deliverable
requested was an *analysis*, not code.

**Done:** measured the developer repo against the declared API surface — three independent measures across
all 1,306 declared endpoint pairs and 6,866 `.cs` files.

**Learned — the finding that redirected the project:**

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Declared endpoints implemented anywhere in `pam/PAM` | **48 of 1,306 — 3.7%** |
| Swagger specs shared by developers | 37 specs, 690 operations |
| Swagger ↔ `APIConfig.java` name overlap | **~6%** — two disjoint surfaces |
| Swagger operations declaring any 4xx/5xx | **0 of 690** |
| Payload helper methods requiring arguments | **0 of 1,099** |

**Outcome:** ⚠️ partially feasible. The objective's *intent* was achievable; its *stated method* — parse the
developer source — was not. A plan built on Roslyn-parsing `pam/PAM` would have failed late.

**Learned (process):** verifying the premise before assessing feasibility was the entire value of the run.

**Also 2026-07-28:** workspace standardized into five top-level folders; `approach/` frozen into
`workbench/archive/`. `GenericScheduler` locked by repeated token attempts (ISSUE-009). Two GET endpoints
stopped the IIS app pool (ISSUE-010) — the earlier runner had continued through **322 consecutive 503s**,
which is why the circuit breaker and pre-flight health probe exist.

heading: 2026-07-29 — chaining proven end to end (3 flows, all PASS)
text:
**Run:** `Reports/Runs/2026-07-29_160155/` — 15 hops, 15 evidence files, zero 5xx.

**Done:** built `chain_runner.py`, a generic executor over **declarative flow JSON** — flows are data, so
generation extends them without touching the runner. Three five-level flows executed live; **UserId 1456**
and **ServiceId 25339** genuinely created and verified by independent reads. ISSUE-009 resolved — the token
failure was a stale password, not a logic fault. All scripts moved to `workbench/scripts/`; auto-delete
removed so every run keeps its own dated folder.

**Learned:**
- ⛔ **`Success: true` does not mean a write happened.** `SetServiceDetails` returns `Success: true` with
  `Message: "Already Exists"` — a no-op that scores green on both status *and* the `Success` flag.
- HTTP 200 carrying `Success: false` + `ErrorCode` captured live; `206-LC_GLD` is absent from the
  framework's `KNOWN_ERROR_CODES {201,202,203}`, so that set is incomplete.
- **Four envelope shapes on one API**, including a bare array with no envelope at all.
- **Blind `Result[0]` chaining fails** — only 19 of 34 LOBs have user groups. Flows must select by name and
  discover the id.
- `ServiceId` is a string on create and an integer on read.
- Writes are slow — creates 5.5–6.5 s. The inherited 2,000 ms SLA was read-only.

**Broke, then fixed:** PowerShell `Get-Content`/`Set-Content` corrupted UTF-8 into mojibake (PS 5.1 reads as
ANSI). **Use the Edit tool for text files.**

heading: 2026-07-29 (later) — full generated run: 326 flows, 1,868 calls, 870 endpoints
text:
**Run:** `Reports/Runs/2026-07-29_181439/` — 3 h 11 m.

**Done:** built `generate_flows.py`; **323 of 326 flows machine-generated**, executor unchanged — which was
the point. 870 distinct endpoints reached (66.6%), 69 of 70 controllers.

**Learned — the headline measurement of the project:**

| | Count | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| Calls issued | 1,868 | |
| Returned HTTP 200 | 1,688 | **90%** |
| **Genuinely passed all seven layers** | **1,204** | **64%** |

**A status-only suite would have reported this run as 90% green. It was 64%.** The 26-point gap is 406
calls, each with a retained evidence file.

Also: **135 × 404** — `APIConfig.java` declares endpoints that do not exist on the deployment. **13 of 217
creates actually inserted.** Eight distinct response shapes, four of them new. Downtime handling worked —
the environment went down three times mid-run and the runner resumed from the paused hop each time.

**Corrected:** the runner's own report said 1,200 passing hops; the true figure is **1,204** — four
bare-array responses were wrongly flagged because generated flows do not emit `envelope: false`.

**Open:** teardown stayed disabled — generated teardown bodies are not bound to the created record's id, so
running them would delete pre-existing QA data. Flow-level verdicts (296 FAIL / 30 PASS) are misleading;
**hop level is the measure to quote.**

heading: 2026-07-30 — the four-source merge
text:
**Done:** `build_source_map.py` merged `APIConfig.java`, the payload helpers, the 2,470-page Confluence API
reference and `pam/PAM` models into `source-map.json`.

**Learned:** 3,194 JSON payload examples parsed, **1,654 bound to an endpoint**; 2,674 property names mapped
to C# types; **only 3 properties carry `[Required]` in the entire product**, so mandatory-ness is always
inferred, never asserted. Create coverage rose to **138 of 217 (63%)** with 27 creates unlocked by
documentation alone. Documentation binds payloads to endpoints **by page proximity**, so some bindings are
wrong — `confidence: medium` is a hypothesis, not a contract.

heading: 2026-07-31 — twelve evidence packs, one ticket raised
text:
**Done:** `Developer-Loopholes/` created — 12 findings, each a self-contained Jira draft plus `EVIDENCE.md`,
`EVIDENCE.xlsx` and machine-readable `data/`, all generated from one dataset by one script so the three
cannot disagree. **`PAMIT-42744` raised** for LH-01.

**Learned:** LH-01 re-validated live — **289 of 289 calls still reproduce, 100%**. Across all findings:
108 distinct error codes against 4 documented; 9 response-shape families; 135 endpoints returning 404;
`SetStatus` exposed over GET on 49 controllers; 23 responses containing credentials; 25 responses ≥100 KB,
largest **8.0 MB**.

**Also:** `GenericScheduler` **locked again**. `POST /arcontoken` now returns
`HTTP 400 {"error":"Your account has been locked..."}`. One request issued, **no retry**. Workaround
established: supply `$env:PAM_API_TOKEN`, which `get_token()` checks first.

**Learned (method):** evidence files are redacted at capture, so a replayed body can carry
`***REDACTED***` where a value was — the redaction is over-broad and also catches booleans. This is why
LH-03's single non-reproducing call was correctly identified as a harness artefact rather than a product
fix. **Never report such a call as "fixed."**

**Open:** LH-02…LH-12 are drafted but deliberately **held**, pending the owner's validation.

heading: 2026-08-03 — structure clarified, instruction mechanism introduced
text:
**Instructed:** the owner set out the intended project structure folder by folder and asked for a review;
then asked for a dynamic instruction mechanism — one file for current instructions, one for permanent
history. **Corrected the same day:** the dynamic file is the *existing* `BLAST/Objective.md`, not a new
`object.md`. A new `object.md` was briefly created and then removed; `BLAST/Objective.md` was restored
byte-for-byte from its archive copy, so no requirement text was lost.

**Decided:** D5, D6, D8, D9 above (D7 reversed).

**Done:**
- Reviewed the stated structure against disk. Confirmed accurate for Dev Project, GitLab repo, Blast,
  Developer Loopholes, Jira, Reports, Workbench.
- Deleted `demonstrate_readme.md` at the owner's request and repointed the 7 links that would have
  dangled. The mention in `BLAST/progress.md` was left in place — that file is append-only history.
- Wired `@BLAST/Objective.md` into `CLAUDE.md` and added a `UserPromptSubmit` hook so edits to it apply
  mid-session. Created this file as its append-only counterpart.
- **Hook implementation note.** `shell: "powershell"` is unusable on this machine — it requires `pwsh`,
  which is not installed (only `powershell.exe`); `jq` is absent too. The hook therefore calls
  `powershell.exe` from the default bash shell, using no `$` variables so bash cannot expand them.
  Two further faults were caught by pipe-testing: PowerShell 5.1 serialises `Get-Content -Raw` as
  `{"value":"…"}` rather than a bare string (fixed with a `[string]` cast), and console output defaults
  to ANSI, which destroys the em-dashes and `⛔` markers (fixed with `[Console]::OutputEncoding`).

**Corrected — four claims in `CLAUDE.md` were stale:**

| Claim | Reality |
|---|---|
| `POST /arcontoken` works | Account **locked** since 2026-07-31 — use `PAM_API_TOKEN` |
| "All four harness scripts" | **Eleven** scripts, including the LH pack family |
| Swagger specs cached under `Reports/SpecCache/` | That folder **does not exist** |
| `workbench/rag/` holds only administrator guides with no schemas | Also holds the 2,470-page API PDF — the best payload source available |

Also documented for the first time: the **IIS app-pool blocklist**, four undocumented top-level folders
(`Developer-Loopholes/`, `jira/`, `required-context/`, `writer/`), and the fact that `Graphify/dev-scope/`
is **marker files only, not built**.

**Open — one unreconciled figure.** How many of the 70 declared controllers are absent from `pam/PAM`:
`CLAUDE.md` said **23 of 70**; `required-context/01-Data-Gap-Analysis.md` and
`workbench/scripts/SOURCE-MAP.md` both say **54 of 70**. The two newer documents agree and cite a basis;
the 23 has no locatable citation. **Not resolved — re-measure before quoting either.** The 48-of-1,306
endpoint figure is not in dispute.

heading: 2026-08-03 (later) — `Objective.md` slimmed to a dynamic instruction file
text:
**Instructed:** keep `BLAST/Objective.md` lightweight — *current active instruction only*. All historical
content moves here and is never copied back. Retire `pending-tasks-in-queue.md`; there is no separate
backlog file, and whatever is in `Objective.md` is the active work. When executing an instruction, use the
whole Dev Project — docs, reports, repos, this file — as context rather than expecting it restated.

**Decided:** D10, D11 below.

**Done:** `Objective.md` cut from ~16.5 KB / 320 lines to a small template. Its outgoing body is preserved
in §5 and the backlog in §6, both below. `pending-tasks-in-queue.md` deleted after archiving.

**Learned (mechanism):** the previous 16.5 KB `Objective.md` exceeded the hook's inline-injection
threshold — the harness spilled it to a side file and injected only a ~2 KB preview. **Keeping the file
small is therefore functional, not just tidy:** under the threshold the full text lands in context on
every prompt, which is the whole point of the mechanism.

| # | Date | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D10 | 2026-08-03 | `Objective.md` holds **active instruction only**. Historical content lives here and is never copied back |
| D11 | 2026-08-03 | **`pending-tasks-in-queue.md` retired.** No separate backlog file — see §6 for its final contents |
| D12 | 2026-08-03 | **Standard CLI workflow adopted** — record the instruction in `Objective.md` *before* implementing; ask ambiguities as MCQ; append outcomes here. Written into `CLAUDE.md` §Standard workflow |
| D13 | 2026-08-03 | Step 2 fires on **substantive task requests only** — not questions, conversational replies, or process changes. A correction **amends** the current instruction rather than replacing it |
| D14 | 2026-08-03 | On overwrite, the outgoing objective is **always appended here first** — including objectives superseded before any work was done |
| D15 | — | **Objective Register adopted** (§0). Every archived objective carries ten mandatory fields under a sequential `OBJ-NNN` ID. Enforced by `CLAUDE.md` §Objective lifecycle |
| D16 | — | **No dates in objective records.** The sequential ID is the ordering. **Filesystem paths are exempt** — run folders are identifiers, and stripping them would break the traceability the register exists for |
| D17 | — | The no-dates rule applies **going forward only**. The existing dated log (§4) and decisions D1–D14 stay as written, honouring append-only. Register backfilled as OBJ-001 … OBJ-006 |
| D18 | — | **`CLAUDE.md` split into path-scoped rules.** Detail that applies to one area moved to `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` frontmatter, loading on demand. Root file cut 523 → 387 lines. **Safety rules stay unconditional** — a rule that only loads after you open a matching file is useless for preventing the first destructive call |
